articles.title_orig: Latest Windows updates bring major NTLM improvements
articles.title_zh: Latest Windows updates bring major NTLM improvements
articles.content_orig:
Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month’s Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws — including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook — and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe , Apple , Google and Mozilla .
Image: Shutterstock.com. Diorama by @zepp1969.
November’s patch release from Redmond tackles 1,093 vulnerabilities, fixing 63 “critical” flaws that can be exploited to seize control over a Windows system with little or no help from users. Nearly half of those critical bugs are remote code execution vulnerabilities. Overall, 535 of the flaws addressed this month allow an attacker to elevate their privileges on a vulnerable device.
This latest round of updates means Microsoft has shipped more than 5,100 security patches so far this year, a staggering number considering that a year ago Microsoft was averaging around 100 patches per month. Microsoft credits advances in artificial intelligence for helping to find (and fix) such a large volume of security bugs in recent months. Last month, Microsoft pushed more than 1,400 fixes.
According to Redmond, just one of the flaws is already seeing active exploitation: CVE-2026-124194 , a spoofing bug in Outlook. The advisory for CVE-2026-124194 says it affects Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise and editions of Microsoft Office .
Several other major software makers pushed security updates this week to fix critical weaknesses in their products. Apple on Monday released out-of-cycle security updates to fix at least nine vulnerabilities in iOS/iPadOS , macOS , watchOS and visionOS . Among the weaknesses reportedly fixed in Apple’s release include an iMessage flaw that could let a remote attacker join a group chat and receive its messages; the updates also fix a separate iMessage flaw that could let someone added to a group access messages sent before they joined.
Lee Neely , an instructor at the SANS Institute , noted that Apple backported the fix to iOS 18.
“I take notice when Apple releases fixes to more than two versions,” Neely wrote in a SANS newsletter today. “You really need to get to version 27.2.1 of their OSes and push folks who are holding onto devices which cannot run the current version. The best plan often involves setting an upgrade date for old hardware. Run through all your Apple devices and make sure everything is up to date, don’t assume the fixes went out automatically.”
Google this week released Chrome version 157.0.8103.50 , which resolves nine security holes, including CVE-2026-125350 , the sixth zero-day vulnerability this year for Chrome (this bug also is being patched in Chromium-based browsers like Edge). The latest Chrome version follows its November 3 release, which fixed 213 vulnerabilities. A new version of Mozilla Firefox out today ( Firefox 160 ) resolves almost 100 CVEs, about half of them high severity.
Adobe today released patches for at least 110 vulnerabilities across a range of products, with nearly half of the flaws rated high severity. Adobe said there is no evidence any of the security holes it addressed this month are being actively exploited.
Chris Goettl , vice president of product management at Ivanti , said it’s easy for security teams at large enterprises to feel overwhelmed by the volume and criticality of patches from Microsoft lately. But he notes that while some 95,000 vulnerabilities have been assigned CVEs this year across all vendors, only 217 have so far this year been added to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) list maintained by the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA).
“Roughly four in ten of this year’s exploited vulnerabilities sit in operating systems, endpoint software, browsers, and server platforms, which a continuous patch strategy can close quickly,” Goettl said.”The rest calls for exposure management alongside patching, especially the 44% that sit in edge devices and IT management or remote access tools, the internet-facing systems that hold privileged access. Teams that can quickly identify those assets, confirm exposure and act on confirmed exploitation can focus on the small slice of vulnerabilities attackers are actively using, while the rest stays on the normal patch cadence.”
Please don’t neglect to back up any important data if you haven’t recently; generally speaking, this is a task best accomplished before applying operating system updates. As ever, if you experience any issues installing this month’s bundle of love from Microsoft, please drop a comment about it in the space below.
Thank you as always.  Your concern and actions for others is very much appreciated by all, including those not aware of it. With respect, John Royal
I wonder whether a goal of a bug-free Windows is mathematically possible, or whether there will always be residual “bugs” in the form of some marginal configurations and conditions that can never be made fully fault-safe.
I’m sure it’s possible to have bug-free software, but I’ve never seen it in anything but very simple programs.  There are ALWAYS bugs.  (I worked in software QA/testing for 20 years…)
There WERE always bugs because humans are fallible, easily distracted, of differing skill level, etc..  Machines will eliminate 99.9% of all bugs moving forward.
How will we know? Will we have to ask the machines?
well, if that wasn’t sarcastic, Jojo, it should be.  Think of an AI coder as a very fast intern-level coder who copies and pastes a lot.
Excellent reporting, as usual. Thank you BK.
Well, if nothing else AI has created a mess of monthly updates on many platforms now. Some crazy times for sure.
I’m waiting for someone to write a story about how closing all these bugs has cut-off ways that the world’s 3-letter spy/security agencies took advantage of and how they are now more constrained at gaining intelligence.
All these fixes should also make hacking a lot more difficult.
Nearly eleven hundred vulnerabilities in one Patch Tuesday is a good moment to ask how any IT shop is supposed to prioritize. The teams that cope best treat patching as a budgeting problem – fixed maintenance windows, explicit risk acceptance for the long tail, and surge capacity reserved for the exploited entries – rather than trying to clear the whole list every month. Reading the details of what got fixed matters less than knowing which of your exposed services map to the CVEs that are already being scanned for in the wild.
Question:  Are all of these “fixes” ONLY in Windows 11 and its associated products? Or, are they counting other Windows versions and their associated products?
I uninstalled Adobe Reader from my computer the other day because it uses AI by default. It was telling me “this document is complex, do you want me to simplify it for you”? How would they know if they hadn’t already read it.
So, following the principle of removing any app that I am not actually using, and don’t really need, I uninstalled it.
Now I have an additional reason to be satisfied with that decision.

Sharma made the announcement on social media while highlighting that Wolfenstein is "one of gaming's most important franchises", and the third entry is once again being helmed by Bethesda studio MachineGames.
Here's a look at her post with an accompanying teaser image:
Prior to this, the Xbox CEO also revealed that Bethesda studio id Software has begun work on its next game, while also hyping up a new "Slaughter Mode" update coming to DOOM: The Dark Ages Revelations next week.
The Verge editor Tom Warren reckons id Software's next title will be another entry in the DOOM series:
It sounds like both of these projects are still very much in their infancy as things stand, although it was rumoured back at the start of 2026 that performance capture was set to begin on the next Wolfenstein title .

articles.title_orig: Megaspeed ex-CEO Alice Huang barred from Singapore amid Nvidia saga
articles.title_zh: Megaspeed ex-CEO Alice Huang barred from Singapore amid Nvidia saga
articles.content_orig:
Singapore’s government said on Thursday the United States had provided little help in its investigation into Alice Huang, the woman at the center of a spy plot that has led to the investigation of Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang .
Singaporean authorities held Ms. Huang’s passport to prevent her from leaving the country from June 2025 until February over “potential false declarations” in relation to her company, Megaspeed, which is based in the country, the government said in a statement. She was ultimately released with a “stern warning” and barred from re-entering Singapore.
The statement raises new questions about the response of the Trump administration to the case and why the U.S. government did not more forcefully intervene. According to the timeline in the statement, Singaporean authorities had been holding Ms. Huang’s passport well after President Trump was briefed last fall about her relationship with Nvidia’s chief executive and the belief that she was a Chinese intelligence asset.
The New York Times has reported that Taiwan began monitoring Ms. Huang in 2024 at the guidance of the U.S. government.
In its statement, Singapore said that it had sought information from an American server maker and close Nvidia business partner, Supermicro, but that the company had provided “limited cooperation.” Supermicro, a firm that packages Nvidia’s A.I. chips onto servers that can be used in data centers, has been at the center of a number of chip smuggling investigations across the globe.
Supermicro was a supplier to Megaspeed, a company incorporated in Singapore and run by Ms. Huang, according to two people with knowledge of the matter.
Singapore said in the statement its authorities raised Supermicro’s “limited cooperation” with the U.S. Department of Justice and Federal Bureau of Investigation in July 2025 and “requested their assistance in securing the company’s cooperation.”
“Despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance in respect of the company,” the statement said.
Supermicro denied that Megaspeed had ever been a customer. “Supermicro did not sell any products to Megaspeed and has operated in compliance with all applicable U.S. export and re-export control laws,” the company said in a statement.
During questioning, Ms. Huang sought to downplay her role in Megaspeed, according to Singapore’s statement. She was ultimately released because of “insufficient evidence relating to the possible inaccurate declarations for which Megaspeed was being investigated.”
She was issued a “stern warning” and barred from re-entering Singapore. The country’s police are continuing to investigate Megaspeed.
Paul Mozur is the global technology correspondent for The Times, based in Taipei. Previously he wrote about technology and politics in Asia from Hong Kong, Shanghai and Seoul.

articles.title_orig: Tim Scott summons Jensen Huang, Howard Lutnick to testify over Nvidia saga
articles.title_zh: Tim Scott summons Jensen Huang, Howard Lutnick to testify over Nvidia saga
articles.content_orig:
Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive, and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick have been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee as Mr. Huang’s affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy raises national security concerns.
Senator Tim Scott, Republican of South Carolina, on Thursday evening sent letters to Mr. Huang and Mr. Lutnick requesting their testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee.
“Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive U.S. technology,” Mr. Scott said in a social media post, adding, “The American people deserve answers.”
Congressional leaders of both political parties have said they support efforts to hear from Mr. Huang directly about his entanglement with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman who U.S. officials concluded had been recruited by China’s main spy agency .
Mr. Scott asked Mr. Huang to appear on Dec. 3 by his own volition but also threatened that the committee could issue a subpoena. House Republicans also said on Thursday they were in discussions with Mr. Huang to testify before other committees. Mr. Huang has hired lawyers who previously represented executives in government investigations, according to people familiar with the matter.
Mr. Huang resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive on Thursday. But that has not appeared to slow a bipartisan push for more information on whether he had compromised national security.
Senator Chuck Schumer of New York, the Democratic leader, said in a social media post that Congress must “demand answers” from Mr. Huang. Mr. Schumer also called on the Trump administration to “answer for what it did once it learned about Mr. Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.”
Mr. Lutnick’s department was required to review companies for national security risks before the Trump administration allowed Nvidia to sell advanced chips to China last year. The top Democrats on two congressional committees also wrote to Mr. Lutnick on Thursday, saying they were investigating the matter.
Senator Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, the top Democrat on the banking committee, said that Mr. Huang’s resignation “does not absolve him, other executives or the company as a whole of responsibility for putting our national security at risk or for any potential violations of our laws.”
She added in a statement that the company still would “owe Congress answers.” She also demanded that Trump officials “ensure our advanced technology is not fueling China’s military.”
Michael Gold , Ana Swanson and Tony Romm contributed reporting.

articles.title_orig: Microsoft Outlook outage stretches on for hours - ABC News
articles.title_zh: Microsoft Outlook outage stretches on for hours - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
The company posted about the disruptions on social media.
Microsoft said it was working to restore service as a widespread outage of Outlook email and other products stretched on for hours Thursday.
"We’re seeing positive results with our efforts to restart affected infrastructure and recover server availability in an isolated manner. We’re actively monitoring the performance of these portions of infrastructure to verify stability, which we suspect will support improved availability as these actions are subsequently expanded more broadly," the company wrote in an update on X.
Downdetector , which monitors outages, reported issues with Outlook, Teams and other products on Thursday, as Microsoft attempted to deploy several fixes.
Amid the Outlook outage, the company said that some infrastructure was "experiencing elevated load across multiple regions" due to strain from a "number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable."
"We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact," the company said. "We've paused all deployments, we're moving additional traffic off the affected infrastructure, and we're restarting affected servers to return them to service."
In the ensuing hours, Microsoft has detailed actions it has taken to try to bring servers back to service, some of which it said did not provide the "anticipated relief."
Around 6 p.m. ET Thursday, the company said it was "returning a portion of affected servers to the service, and they remain stable so far," though later updated that the servers "can become unresponsive again once they receive traffic" and was working on a fix for that.
Earlier, Microsoft also reported some users were experiencing issues with Microsoft Teams. The company shortly updated that "mitigative actions have successfully restored service health and functionality."
Amid the outage, New York City's Emergency Management Department warned residents of potential delays in reaching city agencies.
"If you are trying to contact a New York City agency by email or access an online City service that relies on Microsoft systems, you may experience delays or temporary disruptions," NYC Emergency Management said on social media. "These issues may affect the delivery of emails, responses from City agencies, and access to certain online services."
For more urgent requests, the city advised residents to try using an alternative method to contact the agency, and to call 311 for non-emergency city services and 911 for emergencies.
This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

articles.title_orig: Was This New Fable Gameplay Meant to Sell the Game?
articles.title_zh: Was This New Fable Gameplay Meant to Sell the Game?
articles.content_orig:
I am pretty confident Fable will be a fantastic RPG when it finally releases in February 2027, but for those still sat on the fence, Xbox is going to have to do a better job of promoting it than this latest example.
To mark the 25th anniversary of Xbox, four minutes of gameplay taken from a quest has been uploaded. However, all of maybe 30 seconds of it actually has anything going on. Watch it above.
Obviously, you do indeed do a lot of walking during open world RPGs, but it's not something you usually feature much in marketing beats. That's what most of the latest gameplay slice for Fable is, though: walking.
Subscribe to Push Square on YouTube 172k
Partway through, there is a combat sequence showing off swordfighting, archery, and magical abilities. It's over quickly, however, and then we're back to walking. The video then concludes with a cutscene lacking context as it's been plucked out of the full game to be seen online.
I grew up playing the three mainline Fable games on the Original Xbox and Xbox 360; I have very fond memories of this series, so I want the new rebooted instalment to do well. It'll need better presentations and trailers than this for a good chance at that. It's out for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC on 23rd February 2027.
What do you make of the video? Share your thoughts in the comments below.
Liam grew up with a PlayStation controller in his hands and a love for Metal Gear Solid. Nowadays, he's found playing the latest and greatest PS5 games as well as supporting Derby County. That last detail is his downfall.
I am sure that this going to be a good game
I am very excited for Fable but I must admit the combat always looked janky since they first showed it off.
Edit: also going to throw this out there, First party Sony games get stick for having slow walking section... just an observation
Yeah, I think they couldve chosen a more exciting part of the game to highlight. It’d be like the Spider-Man 2028 trailers featuring clips of Peter walking about FEAST.
The combat section looked really good here I thought. Why did they want to show off that the game has a load of walking in it?
Looks boring and don't tell me that's the fastest you can run. Can't sprint?
It's probably meant to be a graphical showcase and narrative tease. Doesn't mean it's good — and, more than anything, it was probably thrown together in a few days because daddy Microsoft abruptly told them to make a trailer for Xbox's anniversary.
But...I dunno. I wouldn't give them too much flack for it. I certainly wasn't aware of this trailer before reading this article, so I doubt it has much gravitas to it or is intended to sell the game to a wide audience. Just some subpar marketing from the studio that is pretty bad at marketing.
All I can assume is it’s an attempt to be a graphical showcase. Which doesn’t do much for me because it’s so much less stylised than previous games in the series and looks more like a new Hellblade than a new Fable. I dunno, I still don’t think the general tone of that headline would be the same if this was a PS exclusive and not an Xbox game. Do we remember the GoT trailer during a state of play that was like 6 or 7 minutes of walking before any combat?
I just have that feeling it’s not going to be all that. I’m just doing my Zelda OOT play through and watched the fable trailer. Unfortunately the trailer did absolutely nothing for me compared to what I was playing and enemies I was fighting and combat in OOT. Apart from FH6 I don’t think their studios are capable for whatever reason of producing a game of OOT quality etc.
@RoomWithaMoose you nailed it. Definitely a last minute "trailer". They've already shown all they need to, and this trailer doesn't do any help nor harm at this point. That being said, it still looks good to me ,and I'm stoked for the return of Fable proper after all these years.
It looks like a technical demo that should have stayed in-house and should never have been used to showcase the game for a public presentation. I'm still going to play the game.
Why do Xbox studios games of late environments look so static. Gears e day was like it and fable seems the same. No areas where there are trees and bushes blowing in the hard wind, rain lashing down, soaking wet floors, massive snow falls, you get the idea. Gears and fable environmentally look ok but dull very slight breeze and very minimal object foliage movement etc in all areas.
Did you not know? Xbox pioneered walking in video games!
But seriously, I'm just gonna ignore that this video was even put out. Every game has slow sections, it can't be all flashy set pieces and bombastic action, especially in a narrative-driven RPG. I'll just wait to see more gameplay and the reviews when they come out at launch.
Yeah not a great showing this, I agree. Although overall I'm still looking forward to the game.
@AI-Generation also replaying OoT and forgot how seminal and sublime it is. I’m not sure many are capable of producing something like that even 28 years after the OG came out!
Im sure the full game will be great, I'm genuinely looking forward to it. But that trailer really gave me some DA Veilguard vibes and thats not a great thing :/
As others have said, I think this was meant to be a graphical showcase. I’m sure they’ll be a “gameplay” trailer closer to release. My most anticipated game even over GTA VI!!!
The game isn't out for another 3 months so I'm sure they'll cook up more gameplay videos by then.
Glaring at Bethesda At least they showed SOMETHING.
Still looking forward to it
Reminded me of the majority of the GoW Laufey reveal. I don’t get why games continue to get showed off like this nowadays when graphical improvements are giving diminishing returns, made much more sense over a decade ago certain games would be a clear graphical leap.
Liam, come on man. Is this an article for clickbait. The Sony MS war is over. Sony won. There are many other videos of the gameplay. Why stir the flames for your crowd? Can people get over the console wars at this point?
You just know even after every Sony misstep, at the end of the day, they walk into the last conference room for the night and go ‘still, at least we aren’t Xbox.’ And have a good laugh.
I'm still gonna buy it 'cause I like what I see so far and that it's gonna be my first ever Fable game since I've never owned an Xbox
Not the best showcase for the game. I want to believe for this one, but I’m waiting to see how the game reviews before I jump on it.
None of the fables ever rose above good so unlike the author of the article I do not expect this to be a fantastic rpg not even a little
@UnfishedPlate29 yeah if you ignored all the combat Laufey showed off in that 20 mins
This is just MORE of"this game doesn't look so great..."
It all looks so blah, combat looks floaty and weightless, the landscapes look like generic dogshit
I'm definitely not sold...
This gane looks like it's going to be a complete failure like gears of war
Trailer was fine, shows off the narrative / banter
Never ever played fable but if I can drag myself away from GTA one day I might give it a go
Something feels off about this game.
The fable series has always been overrated garbage. Peter Molyneux was a talentless hack and even though he has nothing to do with this, this game look just as garbage as the rest.

articles.title_orig: White House weighs Commerce Secretary Lutnick's ouster amid Nvidia export concerns, sources say
articles.title_zh: White House weighs Commerce Secretary Lutnick's ouster amid Nvidia export concerns, sources say
articles.content_orig:
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is under fire by critics asking whether his ties to Chinese companies and friendship with Nvidia's ousted CEO Jensen Huang contributed to the federal agency's lack of oversight over billions in Nvidia AI chip sales, CBS has learned.
Before President Trump nominated Lutnick to lead the Commerce Department, Lutnick was the chairman and CEO of Cantor Fitzgerald, a New York investment bank which held about $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock at the time.
Lutnick developed a warm relationship with Huang, who resigned Thursday as reports of a growing number of affairs caused new uncertainty about the world's dominant AI chipmaker. One of Huang's alleged relationships was with Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen Huang), who is believed by the U.S. to be a Chinese spy. She ran Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based company that became one of Nvidia's biggest customers for AI chips and is suspected of illegally shipping Nvidia's most advanced AI chips to Chinese entities, circumventing a U.S. ban.
As commerce secretary, Lutnick took the helm of an agency responsible for policing exports of sensitive technology to adversaries and global rivals.
One way the Commerce Department keeps this information and technology out of the hands of China and other adversaries is by putting foreign companies and individuals on its Entity List . This restricts their ability to access U.S. technology products, and inclusion on the list means that the department believes there's a risk that the entity is involved in activities that are contrary to U.S. national security or foreign policy interests.
In 2024, under the Biden administration, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security launched an investigation into Nvidia's chip sales to Megaspeed to determine whether they were being redirected to China. But according to The New York Times , the probe was abruptly transferred to the Department of Justice. The Justice Department would not comment about the investigation.
The Commerce Department has not added a company to the Entity List since October 2025.
Last week, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Lutnick over the Commerce Department's failure to place Megaspeed on the Entity List, Axios reported.
Chris McGuire, an expert on China and emerging technologies at the Council on Foreign Relations, said, "The real scandal here is the lack of enforcement of export controls."
He added that the Commerce Department had known for as long as a year that Megaspeed was being run by a woman who is believed by the U.S. to be a Chinese spy, "and they did nothing." The New York Times reported that about a year ago, President Trump was briefed on intelligence that suggested that Alice Huang was a Chinese asset and that she had grown close to Jensen Huang.
"Either Lutnick doesn't know how to do his job or he is protecting Huang," McGuire said.
The Commerce Department did not respond to a request for comment.
On Thursday, after Jensen Huang's resignation became public, Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the ranking Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, called on Lutnick and his deputy, Jeffrey Kessler, to "explain why they have not closed export control loopholes." Kessler is the undersecretary who led the Commerce Department's probe into Megaspeed.
Warren urged the two to "act today to ensure our advanced technology is not fueling China's military." In March, Warren wrote to Lutnick to demand the "immediate pausing" of all export licenses of Nvidia chips destined for China.
Questions about Lutnick's own relationship with Chinese state companies have further complicated the ongoing Nvidia crisis.
A financial services firm Lutnick ran, BGC Group, had a 33% stake in a joint venture with China Credit Trust, a Chinese state-owned company whose largest shareholder is the China People's Insurance Company, another state enterprise.
Another firm he ran, Cantor Fitzgerald, is still overseen by his two eldest sons. That firm helped several Chinese companies go public in the U.S. Cantor Fitzgerald was also a key investor in Satellogic, a satellite company that is under contract with a Chinese data science company, Zhong Ke Guang Qi Space, until 2033.
His close China ties emerged as a topic at his Senate confirmation hearing last year. Senators questioned whether he could be unduly influenced by Chinese officials, and how he would safeguard U.S. technology.
Sen. Maria Cantwell, a Democrat from Washington state, grilled Lutnick on potential conflicts of interest with respect to his investments in Chinese companies, and Cantor Fitzgerald's financial interest in Tether, a cryptocurrency company with a large footprint in China.
Other senators asked about how he would safeguard U.S. technology from the Chinese Communist Party.
"How will you address different threats that we see coming from the CCP within these information and technology markets?" asked GOP Sen. Deb Fischer, of Nebraska.
Lutnick promised to be vigilant against threats from China.
"I take a very jaundiced view of China," he said in response to Fischer. "I think they only care about themselves and seek harm to us, and so we need to protect ourselves."
Before he was sworn in as commerce secretary in February 2025, Lutnick resigned from all of his corporate leadership posts, transferring his business empire to his children.
Since his tenure as commerce secretary began, Lutnick and his family's net worth doubled to $7.3 billion, thanks to his indirect stake in Tether, according to Forbes , which valued his holding in Tether at $5.4 billion. The stake, worth $1.7 billion in early 2025, has more than tripled in value.
"Can we be confident that he is looking out for the public interest?" asked Kathleen Clark, a law professor and expert on government ethics at Washington University in St. Louis. "What's going on with him raises a lot of red flags."
Lutnick's friendship with Jensen Huang may also be problematic, Clark told CBS News.
Huang met Lutnick soon after Lutnick began his term as commerce secretary, Huang told podcaster Joe Rogan last year.
"He started our conversation with, 'Jensen, this is Secretary Lutnick,'" said Huang. "'I just want to let you know that you're a national treasure. Nvidia is a national treasure. And whenever you need access to the president, the administration, you call us.'"
Huang added that every time he called the commerce secretary's office, "if I want to get something off my chest, express some concern, they're always available."
Huang also visited with President Trump. He attended a $1 million-per-person dinner at Mar-a-Lago in April 2025. At that time, Huang tried to convince Mr. Trump to lift restrictions on the company's less advanced H20 chip sales to China, according to The New York Times . Less than three months later, in July 2025, Mr. Trump lifted the restrictions. Nvidia's most advanced chip, the Blackwell, still cannot be sold directly to China.
In July 2025, Lutnick posted a photo to Instagram showing Huang in his trademark black leather jacket standing in the Oval Office next to Mr. Trump, who was seated at his desk. Lutnick is also in the photo along with other visitors.
"Great to meet in the Oval Office with Jensen Huang on the very day Nvidia crossed $4 trillion in market cap," the post said.

articles.title_orig: Newsom blasts Trump’s climate retreat as giving China an edge
articles.title_zh: Newsom blasts Trump’s climate retreat as giving China an edge
articles.content_orig:
Gov. Gavin Newsom blasted President Trump’s retreat from the fight against climate change, casting it as a global embarrassment and a squandered opportunity to make domestic manufacturing gains.
“China is cleaning our clock,” Newsom said on the sidelines of the United Nations-backed climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkey. “It’s not just about environmental policy. It’s about influence, it’s about supply chains, it’s about investment. As we walk off the international stage, they’re stepping in, and they’re also stepping in with this new technology.”
Newsom, a potential Democratic contender for the U.S. presidency in 2028, was joined by a phalanx of other governors and mayors at the COP31 summit Thursday. Their presence at the talks was a show of force meant to illustrate the work that cities and states are still doing to decarbonize following the Trump administration’s rollback of emission-limiting regulations and withdrawal from the Paris Agreement.
The U.S. government didn’t send an official delegation to the high-level talks, which have brought together nearly 200 countries. Instead, the country was represented unofficially by other U.S. officials. On Thursday, the group included U.S. Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island, Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz, New Mexico Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham and a number of mayors. A coalition of some 19 U.S. House representatives also are set to participate later this week.
Newsom, however, was by far the most visible representative of the U.S., mobbed by dozens of reporters, activists and onlookers as he inched slowly through the venue Thursday, occasionally stopping for selfies and winning the same kind of acclaim showered earlier in the week on Brazil’s newly reelected President Lula da Silva. “We love you, Governor Newsom,” shouted one observer. “You must be president!” yelled another.
U.S. representatives at the climate talks said they were buoyed by the U.S. midterm elections last week, which ushered Democrats into control of the House and Senate as well as a majority of state governorships.
“We’re doing all of this in our states with no help from Washington,” Walz said, adding that Democratic control of Congress could help facilitate those efforts. Under Trump, the federal government has been “throwing barriers into place,” he said, but “it’ll be very difficult for them to do that now.”
Newsom also said he felt “renewed optimism from the midterms” but remained concerned about two more years of environmental policy under Trump. Democrats can wield fresh power to mitigate “the damage,” he said, but can only go so far.
“Trump’s head is in sand soaked with oil. He’s a wholly-owned subsidiary of big oil and we have been on the receiving end of some of the most aggressive assaults on our climate leadership in our generation,” Newsom said.
During Trump’s second term, the administration has pulled back a host of Biden-era regulations, including a mix of mandates and subsidies that encouraged electric vehicles. That’s imperiling American competitiveness, Newsom said.
“I worry about American automobile manufacturers surviving a decade from now,” Newsom said. “If you care about the future of American manufacturing and of automobile manufacturing, you should care about this issue. And so that’s the message I’m communicating here in the absence of one damn representative from the federal government. We are a footnote yet again at COP and that is a disgrace.”
Leaders of cities and states representing more than 60% of the U.S. economy have used the summit to pledge they’d keep forging forward on climate —including by formally collaborating with United Nations officials in tracking the country’s greenhouse gas emissions.
That pledge came in a joint statement from America Is All In, the U.S. Climate Alliance and Climate Mayors initiatives. Collectively, they represent 24 governors with constituents making up 55% of the U.S. population as well as 350 mayors across 47 states.
The two-week COP31 summit is meant to galvanize a worldwide shift away from fossil fuels, an embrace of more emission-free renewable alternatives and additional conservation efforts. The alliances of state and local leaders committed to working with the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, the treaty and institution undergirding the 2015 Paris accord, without support from the U.S. government. Under a formal process kicked off this year, the U.S. is set to officially exit the UNFCCC next February.
The new effort by cities, states and other leaders will involve elevating data on U.S. progress toward decarbonization by midcentury and ensuring engagement in a “global stocktake” exercise meant to assess how the world is doing in meeting its climate goals. A first global stocktake culminated in 2023 with a recognition the world was badly off track its key temperature target, prompting a pledge at COP29 in Dubai to transition away from fossil fuels. Initial discussions are underway in Turkey on the second stocktake set to conclude in 2028.
UN Secretary-General António Guterres told Bloomberg TV Thursday that he welcomed U.S. subnational action on climate. “The U.S. is not the U.S. government,” he said. “We see the private sector in the U.S. clearly more and more investing in renewables, and we see more and more governors and more and more mayors totally committed to that. And I hope that the U.S. as a whole will become again an important part.”
U.S. state-level policy, market forces and falling technology costs can reduce carbon dioxide emissions by as much as 46% below 2005 levels by 2035, according to a report from America Is All In and the University of Maryland Center for Global Sustainability.

articles.title_orig: Cramer says Jensen Huang betrayed Nvidia shareholders. How to pick up the pieces
articles.title_zh: Cramer says Jensen Huang betrayed Nvidia shareholders. How to pick up the pieces
articles.content_orig:
CNBC's Jim Cramer criticized former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Thursday for putting the chipmaker's future at risk.
"Did he betray you, the shareholders?" Cramer asked. "Yes. End of story."
Huang resigned Thursday morning following reports of an affair with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. Hours later, Reuters reported that he had an "intimate relationship" with a second employee. These revelations came days after Huang admitted to an affair with an executive at a Singapore-based cloud computing company whom U.S. intelligence agencies suspect of spying for China. Longtime CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO of Nvidia. Cramer said Huang's departure was necessary to protect Nvidia from further fallout.
Shares ended Thursday down more than 4%, but at its lows of the morning, the stock was off over 14%. The decline in Thursday's session brings Nvidia's losses this year to 12%.
While questions remain about what comes next for the AI chipmaker, Cramer argued that Nvidia's future extends beyond the executive who helped build it into one of the world's most valuable companies. "There won't be a better Nvidia, just a different one [without Huang]," Cramer said, envisioning a company that is better organized and more disciplined about its investments.
Under Huang, Nvidia built an extensive equity investment portfolio that included a $5 billion investment in Intel in 2025 and a $2 billion investment in AI cloud provider CoreWeave earlier this year. The investments, and many others, were part of Huang's strategy to strengthen Nvidia's position across the AI industry.
During the CNBC Investing Club's Morning Meeting livestream Thursday, Cramer recalled urging Kress to reduce the company's stakes in Intel and CoreWeave, only to be told that Huang preferred to maintain them. Cramer suggested that new leadership could take a more disciplined approach to capital allocation, potentially cashing in on some of those investments and returning the proceeds to shareholders through even bigger stock buybacks.
Cramer expressed confidence in Kress, praising her deep understanding of Nvidia's operations and financials. He argued that the longtime finance chief is well positioned to provide stability as the company navigates the investigations surrounding Huang, which stretch from the boardroom to Washington, D.C.
Nvidia didn't respond to CNBC's request for comment on Cramer's remarks. Heller, the crisis PR firm Huang reportedly hired as early as last year, did not respond to CNBC's request for comment.
Going forward, Nvidia's underlying business remains strong, Cramer said, pointing to its substantial cash reserves and expectations for a robust earnings report Tuesday evening. But he cautioned that even strong quarterly results might not be enough to reassure investors during this time of lingering uncertainty.
Investigations into Huang's conduct and possible violations of U.S. chip export restrictions could result in sanctions that hurt Nvidia's international business. Meanwhile, competitors, including Advanced Micro Devices , are making progress with their own AI chips, potentially threatening Nvidia's market dominance. AMD shares surged almost 6% on Thursday, extending their winning streak to five straight sessions.
Those risks have prompted Cramer to take a more cautious approach to Nvidia stock , particularly after the substantial gains shares have delivered over the years for Cramer's Charitable Trust , the portfolio of 32 stocks managed by the Club. On Tuesday, as Huang's future at Nvidia looked more and more in doubt, the Club downgraded Nvidia to a hold-equivalent rating.
"Don't ever turn a successful investment into an unsuccessful trade," he said, urging longtime shareholders sitting on big gains to consider taking some profits. "You don't want to give up all of your gains if the stock falls further. It fell further today after many of the analysts jumped ship and downgraded the stock from buy to hold. There could be more ahead."
At the same time, Cramer cautioned against giving up on Nvidia altogether, pointing to the company's extensive engineering expertise and multiyear product roadmap as reasons to believe it can continue competing at the forefront of AI without Huang.
The "Mad Money" host also drew parallels to Apple's leadership transition from Steve Jobs to Tim Cook , suggesting that Nvidia could benefit from a similarly capable successor who brings a different management style without sacrificing the company's technological edge.

Alice Huang, the alleged Chinese spy at the center of the Nvidia ( NVDA ) affair scandal, is also reportedly being probed over whether organizations linked to her were involved in an effort to smuggle Super Micro ( SMCI ) products.
According to Bloomberg , the US Attorney's Office out of Manhattan is looking into the matter.
The Department of Justice is already investigating a chip-smuggling campaign related to Huang and her former company, the Singapore-based Megaspeed.
Huang is the woman who allegedly had an affair with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang . She is also suspected of spying for the Chinese government.
Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair, but did not name the woman. He also allegedly had separate affairs with two Nvidia employees . Huang resigned as CEO Thursday.
Super Micro produces servers using Nvidia processors that power AI models and applications.
The company has faced controversy in the past.
In 2020, the Securities and Exchange Commission charged Super Micro with "widespread accounting violations." The company settled the charges after agreeing to pay a $17.5 million civil penalty.
In 2024, short-selling organization Hindenburg Research issued a report calling Super Micro's accounting into question.
The company's accounting firm EY subsequently resigned over concerns about transparency and internal controls over financial reporting.
In March of this year, the United States Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York unsealed an indictment alleging that Super Micro senior vice president of business development and member of the board of directors Yih-Shyan "Wally" Liaw and two others established a scheme to smuggle servers into China .

articles.title_orig: US intel isn’t sure if businesswoman spied on Nvidia for China, doesn’t mean she wasn’t a risk, sources say
articles.title_zh: US intel isn’t sure if businesswoman spied on Nvidia for China, doesn’t mean she wasn’t a risk, sources say
articles.content_orig:
The US intelligence community is still working to understand the relationship between a Chinese businesswoman who had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and the Chinese government, with multiple sources telling CNN that the intelligence collected on her to date does not prove that she was acting as a spy for Beijing.
There is disagreement among US officials about the strength of the evidence that Alice Huang was recruited by the Chinese Ministry of State Security (MSS), the Chinese equivalent of the CIA, to spy on Jensen Huang — and, by extension, on US policymakers.
The FBI has been investigating Huang’s affair for at least a year. But Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday that there are still “no conclusions reached by the Department of Justice, or by me, or by [FBI] Director Patel around who she is or is not.” President Donald Trump also hedged Thursday on whether the US had determined she was a spy, when commentator Stephen A. Smith asked whether Huang was right to have stepped down as CEO.
“Well, the big thing is, was the woman a spy? And I don’t know if that’s been determined yet,” Trump said. “But if the woman was a spy, yes. If the woman was not a spy, perhaps it would be different.”
Some officials at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, including those close to director Jay Clayton, have framed the characterization of Alice Huang as a Chinese spy as not entirely accurate and over-torqued, sources said. And officials at the CIA also are not yet convinced that the intelligence collection on Huang to date, including intercepted communications, proves she was knowingly funneling information back to Beijing, a source told CNN.
Still, some Trump officials told CNN that it strains credulity to believe that she was not acting as an agent of the Chinese government — simply by virtue of the fact that she is a successful Chinese businesswoman working with one of America’s most powerful companies .
Under Chinese national security law, Chinese citizens can be compelled to help gather intelligence on behalf of the Chinese Communist Party. Even if she had not done so yet, given her access to Huang — and by extension, to  Trump — some officials believe she posed a clear counterintelligence risk. But to others, the fixation on Huang’s relationship to the Chinese government has obscured broader questions around the US government’s failure to crack down on the diversion to China of sophisticated technology vital to the AI race.
Alice Huang’s Singapore-based company Megaspeed is a major purchaser of NVIDIA chips. The Department of Justice and the Commerce Department began an investigation into the firm in 2024 — part of a broader probe into an ecosystem of foreign shell companies suspected of diverting restricted Nvidia chips to China, a person briefed on the investigation said.
There are now questions brewing inside the White House over why the Commerce Department did not put Megaspeed on the so-called “entity list,” which restricts trade with companies that may pose a risk to US national security or foreign policy interests — at least while the investigation was ongoing, according to a person familiar.
“An intelligence operation wasn’t necessary to achieve that result,” a former Commerce Department official told CNN, noting that Jensen Huang has publicly advocated for the US to sell more chips to China. The fact that chips might be diverted to China through Megaspeed was, theoretically, a place where China’s interest already coincided with Nvidia’s — and “a regulatory loophole” already allowed it, the former Commerce official added.
Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia on Wednesday, following days of reports that he had had an affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. Reports also emerged on Wednesday night that he separately had an affair with a subordinate at Nvidia.
Democratic Rep. Jim Himes, the ranking member of the House Intelligence Committee, told POLITICO Thursday that he left a classified briefing with senior intelligence officials earlier this week unsure of the nature of Huang’s relationship with the Chinese government.
“What’s the relationship with Alice Huang and the Chinese, and what do we know about what influence or information was traded? Because today, at least, I don’t know,” Himes said.
Last year, when US intelligence officials first learned of the relationship between Huang and Alice Huang, officials across the government immediately wanted to know more — and some began sounding the alarm.
Secretary of State and National Security Adviser Marco Rubio warned in a memo in the spring about Jensen’s relationship with Huang, one source told CNN. But it is unclear how detailed the memo got on how much information Huang was or was not sharing with the Chinese government. Rubio briefed Trump on Jensen Huang and his relationship with Alice Huang aboard Air Force One en route to China in May.
The briefing occurred before Jensen Huang joined Trump in Alaska for the final leg of the trip, a source briefed on the matter told CNN.
Different agencies have continued conducting their own reviews of the intelligence, sources said. One particularly alarming development occurred when US intelligence  obtained communications that appeared to indicate someone with close access to Jensen Huang and Nvidia was the source of information that ended up in Chinese intelligence streams, a person familiar with the investigation told CNN.
The FBI, which is conducting the primary counterintelligence investigation, told lawmakers last year that it was particularly suspicious of Alice Huang’s seemingly overnight career pivot from Chinese State television journalist to businesswoman with an unusually large amount of purchasing power in the Chinese economy, one of the sources said.
That, paired with her close relationship to the then-Nvidia CEO has continued to raise red flags inside the bureau, where the counterintelligence probe remains ongoing, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter.
Definitively linking suspicious behavior by Chinese nationals interacting with the United States to a state-directed spying campaign remains a perennial problem for counterintelligence officials trying to defend against Chinese espionage. It is notoriously difficult to collect intelligence on China, and China routinely compels its private citizens to do its bidding overseas.
When it comes to Chinese spying, the threat is in the eye of the beholder — some officials think the fears are overblown, other officials see a Chinese spy in every encounter.
“A lot of these people are guilty of just being Chinese,” said a former senior counterintelligence official.
But Joshua Hodges, a commissioner on the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission, which investigates how US-China trade and economic ties affect American national security, said that “we’ve seen repeatedly the Chinese are incredibly adept at using people both wittingly and unwittingly.”
“Ultimately, what we typically see is those people, at a certain point in time, recognize that they know who they’re working for and they know the ends that they’re working towards,” he told CNN.
Hodges, who served on the National Security Council in Trump’s first term, noted Huang’s past rhetoric denouncing the phrase “China hawks” as “a badge of shame.”
“That clearly is directed to make people stop talking about the topic,” Hodges said. “You’ve got the biggest, one of the biggest, CEOs in the world attacking people for speaking out about something they care about — that clearly only benefits one country.”
CNN’s Kristen Holmes and Alejandra Jaramillo contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Google’s new Gemini model is better at understanding complicated questions
articles.title_zh: Google’s new Gemini model is better at understanding complicated questions
articles.content_orig:
Google is continuing its elemental AI naming scheme with the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen . These names are less descriptive than the Pro/Flash monikers of earlier releases, but Hydrogen’s purpose is clear: It replaces the faster, more economical Flash models most people in Google’s ecosystem use.
With Google’s recent Argon and Carbon releases, the rollout was staged and began with cybersecurity researchers. Even when general availability began, Google restricted access to users paying for its most expensive AI subscription. The limits for Hydrogen are much more relaxed, with access beginning immediately. This model has replaced Gemini 3.8 Flash across the company’s products.
Google claims that Hydrogen represents a major improvement versus the previous Flash model. It runs in one of four thinking levels (low, medium, high, and the new xhigh), and even in high mode, it’s 2.5 times faster than Flash 3.8. Plus, it reduces “fabricated claims” by more than 5x, according to Google’s analysis. Users will also see gains in code generation, with Hydrogen more than tripling 3.8 Flash’s score in Terminal-Bench. In some cases, Hydrogen even trades blows with Argon. It managed a score of 54 in the popular Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with xhigh mode versus 50 for Argon.
Google believes Hydrogen will be a key part of how developers work with agentic coding tools. While it still positions Argon and Carbon as the best for long-horizon tasks and security, Hydrogen’s speed makes it ideal for generating simpler code and running tests without blowing through token budgets.
Hydrogen is also being integrated with Google Search , which the company says is the biggest update to its AI-powered search tools ever. The new model should better handle long, multipart questions, and the responses in both AI Overviews and AI Mode will have more visual elements. The company also claims Hydrogen’s fan-out search has been tuned to link to more sources, but we’ve heard that from Google before.
Everyone will reportedly get access to Hydrogen in search, but it’s a bit more restricted in the Gemini app and AI Studio. The new model is live for AI Pro and Ultra subscribers, but AI Plus and free users are still stuck with the old 3.5 Flash-Lite model. Developers can plug into Hydrogen via the API at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, which is unchanged from 3.8 Flash. Carbon and Argon are currently $2/$10, but they will go up to $4/$20 starting next month.

articles.title_orig: Cisco Systems Raises Outlook On Soaring Revenue, Profit
articles.title_zh: Cisco Systems Raises Outlook On Soaring Revenue, Profit
articles.content_orig:
Cisco shares rose in extended trading on Thursday after the maker of networking gear reported better-than-expected fiscal first-quarter results.
Here's how the company did compared to LSEG consensus estimates:
Revenue increased 24% from $14.88 billion a year earlier, Cisco said in a statement. Net income rose to $4.6 billion, or $1.14 per share, from $2.9 billion, or 72 center per share, a year ago.
Cisco is trying to gain a foothold in the artificial intelligence buildout after missing out on the early years of the generative AI boom. The company's stock price is up about 35% this year as of Thursday's close, trouncing the Nasdaq, which has gained 9% over that stretch.
Cisco raised its expectation for AI infrastructure revenue from hyperscalers to $9 billion this fiscal year, more than double the figure in fiscal 2026.
"Organizations are turning to Cisco for our trusted, market-defining technology and our expertise to help them scale, secure and optimize their environments for the agentic AI era," CEO Chuck Robbins said in the statement .
For the fiscal second quarter, Cisco said it expects revenue of between $18 billion and $18.2 billion, topping the average analyst estimate of $17.88 billion, according to LSEG. The company is projecting adjusted earnings per share of $1.34 to $1.36, beating the $1.23 average estimate.

articles.title_orig: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
articles.title_zh: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
articles.content_orig:
Huang resigned after two extramarital affairs surfaced, one with an alleged spy.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's stunning resignation from the tech company he co-founded in 1993 comes amid investigations by federal authorities and his own board of directors into allegations that he had multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
Huang, 63, had become a trusted ally of President Donald Trump and an adviser to the president on AI technology, visiting the White House for events more than a half-dozen times between January 2025 and October 2026. This year, he has traveled with Trump on a state visit to China and joined the president during a state visit to Great Britain.
A timeline pieced together by ABC News indicates that Huang and Chinese businesswoman and alleged spy Alice Huang (no relation) have known each other since at least 2024, and that Trump had been briefed twice over the past year on the relationship by intelligence officials and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
June 7, 2024 -- The first known photo of Jensen Huang and Alice Huang emerges of them sitting next to each other at Computex Taipei, the world's largest AI exhibition.
Jan. 31, 2025 -- President Donald Trump meets Jensen Huang for the first time during a meeting at the White House.
May 22, 2025 -- Jensen Huang and Alice Huang are captured on video by Taiwanese news outlet TVBS leaving a restaurant together in Taipei.
Fall of 2025 -- Trump is briefed on U.S. intelligence that Jensen Huang is having an affair with a woman believed to be working for Chinese intelligence, a U.S. official and sources briefed on the matter told ABC News. The president does not take any action at the time, the official and sources said.
Dec. 8, 2025 – Trump publicly announces a major policy change that would allow Nvidia to sell H200 AI chips to China in exchange for the U.S. receiving a 25% cut on the sales.
March 25, 2026 -- Trump appoints Jensen Huang as one of 13 members of the newly established President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology.
April 28, 2026 -- Jensen Huang and his wife of more than 40 years, Lori, are guests at the state visit and state dinner honoring Britain's King Charles.
Spring 2026 -- A classified memo is drafted that warns top administration officials that Jensen Huang has a close relationship with a woman that U.S. intelligence officials believe to be a Chinese spy, sources familiar with the matter told ABC News, confirming reporting in The New York Times.
May 12, 2026 -- Secretary of State Marco Rubio shares intelligence with President Trump on Air Force One showing Jensen Huang is in a relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy, a U.S. official and two sources familiar with the matter have told ABC News. This is the second known time that Trump had been warned about the suspected espionage plot, sources with knowledge of the situation tell ABC News.
Trump's briefing from Rubio, first reported in The New York Times, came shortly before Huang joined the president on a state visit to China, according to the U.S. official and sources. Huang was initially not listed among the CEOs joining Trump's China trip, but he joined the president's entourage in Alaska after news reports noted his absence. Trump later posted on his Truth Social platform that Huang was on Air Force One with him.
Sept. 24, 2026 -- Jensen Huang and his wife, Lori, attend a state dinner at the White House hosted by Trump during Chinese Leader Xi Jinping's state visit to the United States.
Oct. 8, 2026 -- Huang attends the "Golden Age of American Innovation" summit at U.S. Institute of Peace in Washington, D.C., where Trump honors him with a National Medal for Science and Technology and Innovation.
Oct. 29, 2026 -- The New York Times reports that Huang and Alice Huang, an executive at the Singaporean tech company Megaspeed, had a "close relationship."
Oct. 31, 2026 -- The Wall Street Journal reports that intelligence officials in the U.S., Singapore and Taiwan had reason to believe that Alice Huang might be a Chinese spy.
Nov. 8, 2026 -- Jensen Huang releases a memo to colleagues acknowledging "I was unfaithful to my wife." He goes on to say, "I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it." He also apologizes to his colleagues, the Nvidia board, partners and shareholders, saying, "My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility."
Nvidia's board of directors announces it is launching an independent investigation into allegations that Huang "has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort." The board says that while it "has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information."
Nov. 9, 2026 -- Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun tells reporters, "The claim regarding a so-called Chinese spy is completely groundless and pure slander."
That same day, President Trump tells reporters he has spoken to Jensen Huang on the phone. "He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy," Trump says at a press briefing.
Nov. 10, 2026 -- The Republican chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, Rep. Brian Mast, tells ABC News he's prepared to subpoena Jensen Huang if he does not respond to a request from several House Republicans for a closed-door briefing on Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy.
Nov. 11, 2026 -- The New York Times reports that Huang allegedly had a second extramarital relationship with an Nvidia executive who reports to him. The Wall Street Journal reports that Nvidia's Board of Directors is reportedly planning to oust Jensen Huang as the company's CEO.
Nov. 12, 2026 -- Nvidia announces Jensen Huang has resigned as the company's CEO and that Colette Kress, executive vice president and CFO of Nvidia, has been appointed the company's interim CEO as the board initiates a search for a permanent replacement for Huang.

articles.title_orig: Iran unveils new peace demand amid reports of 'shouting match' between Trump, Netanyahu
articles.title_zh: Iran unveils new peace demand amid reports of 'shouting match' between Trump, Netanyahu
articles.content_orig:
Reporting from Abu Dhabi, Fox News Digital examines how the UAE is navigating disruptions to global energy supplies.
ABU DHABI, United Arab Emirates — President Donald Trump met Qatar's prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani, on Monday at the White House as diplomatic efforts to end the war with Iran continue, even as Secretary of State Marco Rubio warns that negotiations remain far from a breakthrough and Tehran signals a willingness to negotiate without yielding to pressure.
The competing messages come as the Strait of Hormuz remains a major source of global economic disruption and regional governments push for a diplomatic solution to a conflict that has subjected Gulf countries to thousands of Iranian missile and drone attacks .
Speaking to reporters Sunday before departing for a G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris, Rubio said there had been little progress in negotiations and rejected the terms put forward by Tehran.
"I wouldn't say we're on the verge of a breakthrough," Rubio said.
RUBIO DEFENDS TRUMP'S IRAN WAR AS NOT 'NECESSARILY POPULAR, BUT NECESSARY'
Cargo is loaded at the Port of Fujairah, as the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran limits marine traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, in Fujairah, United Arab Emirates, May 6, 2026. (Amr Alfiky/Reuters)
He emphasized that Trump prefers a diplomatic settlement but described Iran's demands as unrealistic.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Monday that Tehran was prepared to negotiate an end to what he described as a prolonged state of neither war nor peace.
"We can negotiate with dignity and resolve the issue with dignity. We favor dialogue and negotiations," Pezeshkian said, according to Anadolu Agency on November 9 , citing an Iranian presidential statement.
He said Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei had instructed officials to end the uncertainty but insisted that Iran would not surrender to coercion.
Trump, meanwhile, signaled Sunday that he was not seeking another escalation. In an interview with CBS' "60 Minutes," the president said he saw no reason to intensify the war with Iran while maintaining that the Strait of Hormuz was open.
Mediators have been discussing a two-day proposal under which the United States would lift its naval blockade and release some frozen Iranian funds . Tehran would then take steps toward renewed nuclear inspections and reopen the Strait of Hormuz before broader negotiations resumed, according to Axios on November 9 .
The proposal has not been accepted by Washington, and significant differences remain over the terms of any agreement.
'VAST MAJORITY' OF IRAN'S ATTEMPTED ATTACKS ON STRAIT OF HORMUZ ARE UNSUCCESSFUL, CENTCOM SPOKESMAN SAYS
A satellite image shows the Strait of Hormuz, a key maritime passage connecting the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman, vital for global energy supply. (Amanda Macias/Fox News Digital)
Nowhere are the consequences of the diplomatic stalemate clearer than in the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow shipping corridor connecting the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman.
Before the war, the equivalent of roughly one-fifth of global petroleum liquids consumption and more than one-fifth of global liquefied natural gas trade passed through the waterway, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration , making it one of the world's most strategically important maritime routes.
Since the conflict began, Iranian attacks, shipping restrictions and U.S. military operations have severely disrupted commercial traffic.
Despite the American naval presence, attacks on commercial vessels have continued.
Reuters reported Monday that tanker attacks in the Gulf and Strait of Hormuz had accelerated sharply in October and continued into November. Iranian authorities also claimed that a tanker had struck a mine east of the strait on Sunday.
In an interview with Fox News Digital at the ADIPEC energy conference in Abu Dhabi, Amos Hochstein, a former senior adviser to President Joe Biden and now managing partner at TWG Global, challenged claims that the strait had effectively reopened.
HORMUZ CRISIS HIDES A DEEPER OIL THREAT THAT COULD OUTLAST THE WAR
A view of the Port of Fujairah as U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran limits marine traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, in Fujairah, United Arab Emirates, on May 6, 2026. (REUTERS)
"There has been a hot conflict in the Strait of Hormuz on almost a nightly basis. Tankers are getting fired on, tankers are getting hit," Hochstein said.
"If you need a heavy U.S. military presence just to let an oil tanker go through, to me that's the definition of not open," he told Fox News Digital.
Hochstein argued that the extraordinary security measures required to protect commercial vessels demonstrate that normal navigation has not been restored.
Higher insurance premiums, the danger of additional attacks and restrictions on maritime traffic have continued to burden the global economy.
His assessment contrasts with the more optimistic picture offered by U.S. Central Command. In late October, Adm. Brad Cooper, commander of CENTCOM, said American forces had cleared primary shipping routes of Iranian mines and assisted thousands of commercial vessels transiting the waterway.
According to a CENTCOM statement reported October 25 , more than 3,000 commercial vessels had successfully transited Hormuz with American military support over the preceding six months.
But for Hochstein, the ability of military forces to escort ships does not mean the commercial risks have disappeared.
He suggested that negotiations could proceed on separate tracks, with Washington concentrating on Iran's nuclear program while Gulf governments take a greater role in discussions over freedom of navigation and maritime security.
"Maybe the Gulf allies themselves should be the ones that are managing that part of the negotiation on the [strait] while the United States would manage the negotiations ... on the nuclear front," Hochstein told Fox News Digital.
Dr. Angela Wilkinson, CEO of the World Energy Council, said the disruption of the Strait of Hormuz has exposed the need to rethink global energy markets, which have traditionally prioritized efficiency over resilience.
"Efficiency is not enough. We have to have resilience," Wilkinson told Fox News Digital at ADIPEC.
"What we at the World Energy Council recommend is that we rebalance energy," she said, advocating solutions that address energy security, affordability and sustainability simultaneously.
"We have escalating logistics costs, but we've got new vulnerabilities of interdependency. And that's what we're navigating our way through."
TOP GULF OFFICIAL OFFERS GLIMMER OF HOPE ON TRUMP-IRAN NUCLEAR TALKS AS THREAT OF WAR HANGS OVER REGION
Dr. Ali Rashid Al Nuaimi, chairman of the UAE Federal National Council's Defense, Interior and Foreign Affairs Committee, speaks to Fox News Digital in Abu Dhabi about the Iranian threat, regional security and prospects for diplomacy. (Efrat Lachter/Fox News Digital)
For the UAE, the disruption has accelerated efforts to reduce dependence on the Strait of Hormuz.
The Emirates has invested in alternative routes, particularly its pipeline to Fujairah on the Gulf of Oman, outside the strait, allowing some oil exports to bypass the contested shipping corridor.
Al Nuaimi said the country had substantially increased its oil exports since the war began.
"We want the Strait of Hormuz to be open, to be respected according to international law, but we don't wait and make our country and our people hostages to others. … Before the war started on February 28th, we used to export 3.1, 3.2 million barrels a day. Now we are exporting almost 4.4."
UAE Energy Minister Suhail Al Mazrouei also said at ADIPEC on November 2 that the country's exports had, at times, exceeded prewar levels.
The country is also investing in new export routes, overseas storage capacity and shipping infrastructure to strengthen its ability to withstand future disruptions.

articles.title_orig: Homes aren't selling. Here's the new playbook for selling yours
articles.title_zh: Homes aren't selling. Here's the new playbook for selling yours
articles.content_orig:
Mortgage rates slid for the fourth consecutive week but remain above 7 percent, adding pressure to a bleak housing market struggling with rising prices and declining sales.
The rate on the most popular home loan in the United States, the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage, fell slightly to 7.11 percent, from 7.18 percent the week before, the mortgage finance giant Freddie Mac said on Thursday. The same rate averaged 6.24 percent a year ago.
There was hope that mortgage rates might ease below 7 percent, a psychological threshold that could draw more buyers to the market. But industry experts say that marker is not likely to be breached any time soon.
High housing costs have made buying a home unaffordable for many Americans, said Brad Case, the chief residential economist at Homes.com, a real estate search portal owned by CoStar, a data analytics company.
“I don’t think affordability challenges are going away any time soon,” he added, “because I don’t think we’re likely to see substantially lower mortgage rates.”
Squeezed by high mortgage rates and rising inflation, buyers and sellers are sitting out of the market until conditions improve, which has depressed home sales. Sales of existing homes fell 8.8 percent in October from the year before, and 5.5 percent lower than September’s pace, according to a report released Thursday by the National Association of Realtors, a trade group.

articles.title_orig: Cerebras surges 17% after beating on quarterly revenue and announcing Microsoft deal
articles.title_zh: Cerebras surges 17% after beating on quarterly revenue and announcing Microsoft deal
articles.content_orig:
Cerebras Systems reported better-than-expected results and quarterly guidance in its earnings report on Thursday, and touted a new deal with Microsoft . The stock soared 17% in extended trading.
Here's how the company performed relative to LSEG consensus:
Cerebras' core revenue grew 70% from $135.7 million, compared with 103% growth in the second quarter, according to a statement .
"I think there is opportunity created by, particularly on the hardware side, the sale of hardware, where long lead times in GPUs and more expense creates opportunity for us," Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman told CNBC in an interview, referring to graphics processing units.
Executives will announce a new relationship with Microsoft , one of the world's top cloud providers, on a conference call with analysts, Feldman said. The call starts at 5 p.m. ET.
"We believe revenue begins to show up in Q1 '27," Feldman said in the interview, adding that Microsoft signed the deal in October. Cerebras has also landed deals with other major cloud providers Amazon and Oracle .
Cerebras is evaluating its financing options to meet the ramping demand, Feldman said in the interview.
The company is trying to challenge Nvidia in the AI chip market. Its earnings land on the same day that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned from the company he co-founded after multiple scandals involving extramarital affairs.
For the fourth quarter, Cerebras expects a core gross margin of 47% to 49%, with $310 million to $330 million in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for a 42.1% margin and $271 million in revenue.
Cerebras said it expects revenue to triple in 2027. That implies about $2.85 billion in revenue. Analysts surveyed by LSEG were looking for $2.92 billion.
Cerebras shares have slumped by about 47% since the company debuted on Nasdaq in May.
