articles.title_zh: US Justice Department has not concluded Alice Huang was Chinese spy, Blanche says
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned following reports that he had multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a  suspected agent of China and another with an executive who reported to him — a stunning turn of events for the head of a company at the heart of the global AI investment boom.
Colette Kress, the company’s chief financial officer, will become interim CEO, Nvidia’s board said in a statement.
Nvidia shares plunged more as much as 16% after the board’s announcement, before later recovering and closing lower by 4.3%. A company spokesperson clarified that Huang will not be working with Nvidia in any capacity going forward.
The company also named its first chairman. That role will be filled by Harvey Jones, who is a former CEO of major chip company Synopsys. The addition of a chairman is a major governance overhaul at a company that for decades relied solely on Huang.
Nvidia’s board met Wednesday night to address Huang’s future at the company, a source familiar with the matter told NBC News, adding that the White House was aware of the meeting.
Huang, 63, co-founded Nvidia in the early 1990s and led the company’s meteoric rise amid the AI boom of the past several years.
“I believe deeply in this company and in its future,” Kress wrote in her first email to Nvidia employees as interim CEO. “The Board, Estaff and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period and I want you to know how grateful we are for your resilience, professionalism and continued dedication. Thank you.”
In a separate note to the company’s workforce, Jones, the new chairman, wrote: “The Board takes seriously our duty as stewards of this great company.”
Kress has been the company’s chief financial officer since 2013. She is a familiar face to Wall Street, regularly appearing at conferences and discussing the intricacies of the company’s sprawling operations. Before Nvidia, Kress worked at Cisco, another major technology company, and Microsoft.
Huang long leaned on Kress during financial conferences and the company’s earnings calls to debrief the investing public about the latest developments with the company’s operations.
Nvidia’s board said that it would search for a permanent CEO and consider internal and external candidates.
President Donald Trump weighed in on the search for a permanent CEO shortly after Nvidia’s announcement, saying that Apple executive chair Tim Cook should take the role. “A Legend replaces a Legend!” Trump wrote.
Cook only became Apple’s executive chair on Sept. 1 and did not appear to have plans to leave any time soon.
Kress’ ascension to the CEO role comes after the second largest public company in the world was hit with multiple scandals involving its founder.
On Wednesday, The New York Times , citing five people who worked at Nvidia, reported that Huang had an extramarital relationship with a married healthcare executive who reported to him, which appears to run afoul of Nvidia’s code of conduct. NBC News has not independently verified the claims.
Nvidia and the executive did not respond to multiple requests for comment Wednesday about the Times’ report.
The report concerning the alleged relationship followed reports that Huang had an affair with Alice Huang, a businesswoman believed to be a spy for China. The two Huangs are not related.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio circulated a memo to officials in the Trump administration this spring outlining how U.S. intelligence showed that Huang was in a romantic relationship with a business executive who was an asset of China’s spy service, according to a person familiar with Nvidia and a former national security official with knowledge of the matter. The New York Times and the Financial Times , citing people familiar with the matter, first reported on the memo last week.
Alice Huang held a senior position at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that was buying advanced chips from Nvidia. Megaspeed and other related firms remain under U.S. criminal investigation of allegations they smuggled American-made chips into China.
Alice Huang’s precise role and relationship with China’s spy service is unclear. It is possible she was not a career spy for China’s spy agency, the Ministry of State Security, but was asked to cooperate and share information based on her access to Jensen Huang, according to the former national security official.
The concerns about the Nvidia CEO’s extramarital activity added to worries about Nvidia chips being smuggled or illegally accessed by Chinese AI companies. Nvidia has said that it follows U.S. export laws.
On Sunday, Nvidia’s board announced it was investigating whether Huang had fallen victim to a foreign intelligence plot. It said Tuesday that it had hired a former acting U.S. attorney and his law firm to conduct the investigation.
Huang apologized in a memo to employees and said he supported the independent investigation.
“I was unfaithful to my wife,” he wrote. “My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
Multiple Washington officials have called for greater scrutiny of Nvidia and for Huang to testify about his relationship with the suspected Chinese agent in the wake of the reports.
China has denied the allegations, calling them “purely unsubstantiated and directed at smearing China.”
Through Thursday’s closing bell report, Nvidia shares have plunged about 11 % this week, wiping out $500 billion in value. Huang’s departure leaves a host of unknowns at the company, the valuation of which has soared to more than $4 trillion amid insatiable demand for its GPU chips. Those specialized processors underpin the AI applications that have powered the stock market and economic growth writ large to new heights.
For years, Huang has effectively been the chief ambassador for the artificial intelligence industry, appearing regularly alongside heads of state and other CEOs as the industry spends trillions of dollars investing and building AI models and data centers.
Nvidia acknowledged Huang’s contributions to the sector in its Thursday announcement. “Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound,” a statement said. “The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry.”
After coming up with the idea for Nvidia at a Denny’s restaurant in Silicon Valley with co-founders Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem.
Before Wednesday’s report of a second affair, many high-profile figures across Silicon Valley, Wall Street and Washington had come to Huang’s defense. Trump told reporters Sunday that Huang had “done an amazing job for our country.”
“I think he’s an honorable guy,” Trump said. “I think he probably has an excuse for it. You have to hear it.”
Shaun Maguire, a partner at the venture capital group Sequoia, said on X that Huang is “one of the greatest entrepreneurs of this generation,” adding that “two mistakes don’t make a right, and I believe Jensen is irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership.”
SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk responded under Maguire’s post, writing: “I agree.”
Before the decision, Musk said in a response to a post Wednesday night that it “would be an honor” to hire Huang.
Rob Wile is a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist covering breaking business stories for NBCNews.com.
Steve Kopack is a senior reporter at NBC News covering business and the economy.
Brian Cheung is a business and data correspondent for NBC News.

articles.title_orig: Netanyahu-Eisenkot briefing reportedly told IDF sees no urgent need to strike Iran
articles.title_zh: Netanyahu-Eisenkot briefing reportedly told IDF sees no urgent need to strike Iran
articles.content_orig:
Netanyahu to brief Yashar leader on current security situation following Eisenkot’s request, in the absence of an opposition leader
(Gil Cohen-Magen/picture alliance via Getty Images)
Yashar Party leader Gadi Eisenkot speaks to the press ahead of a party meeting at the Knesset in Jerusalem on the opening day of the new parliamentary session.
Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot warned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that starting a major security operation while coalition talks are ongoing would violate the public’s trust, and sought to compel Netanyahu to brief him on national security.
Eisenkot sent Netanyahu a letter on Wednesday demanding that he “act with national responsibility at this sensitive time. Exercise restraint and caution regarding dangerous actions that can wait until a new government that has secured the confidence of the Knesset is sworn in. Do not violate the public’s trust in the institutions of the government and in the decision-making process.”
Negotiations to form a governing coalition led by Eisenkot officially began this week, amid ongoing U.S.-Iran tensions and Israeli strikes in Gaza.
Eisenkot’s letter comes after Israel’s Channel 12 reported on Wednesday that IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir opposed actions Netanyahu sought to have the military carry out against Iran, in light of the current political uncertainty and U.S. President Donald Trump’s apparent lack of enthusiasm for a renewed war with Tehran following the Republicans’ major losses in the midterm elections.
“The use of the security forces in the absence of a direct and immediate threat requiring action without delay could have devastating consequences for Israeli democracy and citizens’ trust in the institutions of government,” Eisenkot stated in the letter. “You must not place the heads of the security establishment in a grave constitutional dilemma or leave them in doubt about what is required of them and the right course of action. Allow them to uphold, without doubt, the sacred duty entrusted to them.”
In a speech to the Knesset this week, Netanyahu said that “Iran is acting to renew the nuclear threat. The only way to remove this existential threat forever is to bring down the ayatollahs’ regime. We will soon face international pressures to accept a nuclear Iran and the existence of the terror regime that seeks to destroy us… Facing these threats, we must do one thing in this house: Put aside all other considerations and establish a national unity government.”
Netanyahu remains prime minister until a new government is sworn in; while the opposition calls him a “caretaker prime minister,” no such legal designation exists in Israel. The outgoing government is not constrained by law in actions it can take, though there have been legal precedents regarding reasonable actions such a government may take, especially with regard to budgetary allocations. Outgoing governments have started military operations in the past, such as the 2008, 2012 and 2019 Gaza operations, the latter two of which were under Netanyahu’s leadership.
The Prime Minister’s Office responded to Eisenkot that “every decision made by the government led by Prime Minister Netanyahu was made for security reasons only and in full coordination with the security establishment. They brought unprecedented achievements to the State of Israel and will continue to do so in the future.”
“Instead of sowing fear and separation, we must behave responsibly,” the PMO statement read. “Eisenkot’s letter is an irresponsible move … It is a transparent attempt to bring politicization to the matter of Israel’s national security.”
Netanyahu’s office accused Eisenkot of “trying to establish a government with terror supporters” — as the prime minister has called Arab parties in recent weeks — and called for Eisenkot to form a coalition with him.
Defense Minister Israel Katz said on Thursday that the government does not “need approval from the opposition or any legal authority to direct the IDF to carry out assassinations in Gaza, defensive operations and strikes in Lebanon, maintain the security zone in Syria to protect communities in the Golan, clear a terrorist neighborhood in Hebron.”
“With regard to Iran, we have demonstrated resolve and sound judgment, in full coordination with the IDF, and this will continue to be the case … Israel’s security is not on hold and not waiting for the political processes that are taking place in parallel,” he stated.
Eisenkot sent a second letter to Israeli Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara asking her to order Netanyahu to hold regular security briefings with him “to ensure effective oversight, uphold a proper national decision-making process and safeguard national security interests.”
By law, Israel’s prime minister must brief the opposition leader on national security each month. However, as there is no governing coalition, there is currently no opposition leader whom Netanyahu must brief.
Eisenkot argued in the letter, “in the absence of a new opposition leader, and as the person entrusted by the President of the State with the mandate to form a government, it is appropriate that [he] receive regular, structured and comprehensive security briefings, as well as access to intelligence assessments.”
He also wrote that his team has attempted to arrange such meetings with the prime minister, to no avail.
On Thursday morning, Netanyahu and Eisenkot’s offices announced that they will meet for a security briefing, with the prime minister’s military secretary, Maj. Gen. Guy Markizeno, in attendance.
Netanyahu and his allies in the Knesset have also reportedly attempted to prevent the Knesset Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee, which has oversight over the IDF and Mossad, from convening. Following the new Knesset’s inauguration on Tuesday, Eisenkot’s bloc moved to place its members at the helm of major Knesset committees, including Yisrael Beiteinu leader and former Defense Minister Avigdor Liberman as chairman of the Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee.
Liberman wrote on X on Thursday morning that “a caretaker government cannot make decisions that could drag Israel to war without parliamentary oversight and without the full agreement of all security agencies. I emphasize: all security agencies.”

articles.title_orig: Nvidia live updates: Jensen Huang had ‘intimate relationship’ with second employee, Reuters reports
articles.title_zh: Nvidia live updates: Jensen Huang had ‘intimate relationship’ with second employee, Reuters reports
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down as CEO of the chipmaker he co-founded 33 years ago and built into a $4 trillion company that powered the artificial intelligence boom, the company announced Thursday.
CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO.
"The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," said board chair Harvey Jones in a release announcing the news.
The company will begin the search for a permanent CEO to replace Huang and will consider both internal and external candidates, according to the release.
Kress also provided a statement in the release, but Huang was not quoted.
After a meteoric rise to fame due to Nvidia's central role in AI, Huang's dramatic fall has been even more rapid, following a series of stinging revelations about his romantic ties to a woman believed by the U.S. intelligence community to be a Chinese spy.
Huang, 63, apologized on Sunday for being "unfaithful to my wife," though he provided no details about the affair with businesswoman Alice Huang, who has worked for a Chinese company and Nvidia customer called Megaspeed. Late Wednesday, The New York Times reported that the Nvidia CEO also had a separate affair, this one with Kimberly Powell, vice president of health care at the chipmaker. Later that afternoon, The Times and other outlets reported that Nvidia's board met to discuss the company's future.
Huang's downfall also puts the spotlight on President Donald Trump , who formed a particularly close relationship with the CEO of what, until recently, was the world's most valuable company. Huang became a key voice on U.S. AI policy while pushing for issues that were in Nvidia's interest, such as preserving access to open-source AI, and lobbying to allow chip exports to China.
President Trump lamented the "horrible thing" that happened to Huang in an interview conducted hours after his close corporate ally resigned as Nvidia's CEO.
Trump referenced Huang after telling conservative commentator Hugh Hewitt that the U.S. would be in "bad shape" if it lost its edge in artificial intelligence.
"I've seen it. I study it. I'm genetically blessed. I have an uncle that was probably considered the number one professor in the history of MIT for 51 years," Trump said.
"He was there, and he got the science award, the same award that I gave to Elon [Musk], and you know, I gave them out last week. We gave it to Google. We gave it to a lot of great people ... we gave it to Jensen," he said.
"Frankly, that was a little before. But what a horrible thing that is! That's so sad to see that happen," Trump said. "But my uncle got the same award from Ronald Reagan. They presented it to me when when I was there last week, and it was sort of something. So I do have, I think, an inclination. I'm a believer in that, you know."
The woman at the center of Jensen Huang's spy-sex scandal may have owned stakes in businesses in China that benefited Huawei, Nvidia's biggest competitor in Beijing, according to findings from private intelligence firm Tesari shared exclusively with CNBC .
Alice Huang was described as a top executive at Singaporean tech company Megaspeed in initial reporting from The New York Times revealing U.S. officials had concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset.
Jensen Huang on Sunday copped to an extramarital affair with an unnamed woman, following numerous additional reports about his close relationship with Alice Huang.
The connections uncovered by Tesari may raise questions about Alice Huang's intent and conduct in her relationship with the ousted Nvidia chief , and whether Jensen Huang knew his romantic partner was closely connected with his competition.
Click here to read the full report.
— Eamon Javers and Kevin Breuninger
Two of Huang's kids, Madison and Spencer Huang, work at Nvidia. So does Madison's husband, Nico Caprez.
Caprez has risen quickly through the ranks, becoming vice president of global AI infrastructure in January, after joining Nvidia as a corporate development manager in 2024. He was previously an alpine skier and consultant with Boston Consulting Group, and met the CEO's daughter in business school.
Madison joined Nvidia as an intern in 2020 after training as a professional chef, then obtaining a Masters of Business Administration from the London Business school. She serves as a senior director of product marketing for the company's robotics division.
Spencer also works in robotics, serving as the director of product management. He joined Nvidia in 2022 as a product manager in the company's Isaac Sim Cloud division after obtaining an undergraduate degree from Columbia College Chicago and an MBA from New York University's Stern School of Business.
In an all-hands meeting last year, Jensen Huang was asked by employees about nepotism. In a recording of this meeting heard by CNBC, he said that hiring children of Nvidia employees "is a good idea if it's done properly, if it's done on merits." He said he was proud of his kids, and added that children of Nvidia executives working at the company were "even better than their parents."
— Lora Kolodny and Isabel O'Brien
Huang had an "intimate relationship" with a second Nvidia employee, Reuters reported, citing two people familiar with the matter.
A day earlier, The New York Times reported that Huang had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company's vice president of health care. Huang on Sunday admitted to one affair following reports of his intimacy with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, reportedly believed by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy.
Reuters is not naming the second employee. Nvidia did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.
Jensen Huang's rise, becoming a "monarch" that was essentially "co-branded so that you can't separate" the CEO from the company, was a corporate governance problem, according to Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, senior associate dean for leadership studies at Yale School of Management.
"There are a lot of times [corporate boards] are beholden," Sonnenfeld told CNBC's Morgan Brennan on "Morning Call." "They're smitten by the CEO; kind of idolatry."
Nvidia's board reflects that. Prior to his exit on Thursday, Huang was one of 11 members of the board, which had no chair. None of Nvidia's 10 other board members are current or former S&P 500 CEOs. On average, they've been on the board for 15 years.
Across the S&P 500, the average tenure of an independent director is 7.8 years and roughly one in every four directors is a former CEO, according to 2025 data from the Conference Board . Sonnenfeld said "no one was equipped to step in."
"Somebody needs to ask some questions, and that's what's missing here," he said.
Rep. Bill Huizenga of Michigan, Vice Chair of the House Financial Services Committee and a Republican, said it would be "helpful" if Commerce Department Secretary Howard Lutnick testified to Congress in public, in the wake of reports that he stalled a crackdown of firms routing Nvidia chips to China by President Donald Trump .
"They have not been as cooperative as they should be. They have not been as transparent with Congress, much less I think others within that system," Huizenga said of the Commerce Department Thursday. "I want to hear from them a commitment and a recommitment to national security and making sure that these very important technologies and pieces of equipment and chips and other things aren't falling into the wrong hands."
Huizenga told CNBC the Bureau of Industry and Security, a subagency of Commerce that handles export controls, needs to take Congressional concerns about the export of Nvidia chips to China seriously.
"The notion of being able to slow this down and be more selective is actually a positive thing, and what I mean by [that is] not slowing down the technology, but slowing down that transfer of technology," he said.
The Financial Service

articles.title_orig: Lutnick Under Fire Over Huang’s Nvidia Exit—After He Allegedly Blocked Megaspeed Crackdown
articles.title_zh: Lutnick Under Fire Over Huang’s Nvidia Exit—After He Allegedly Blocked Megaspeed Crackdown
articles.content_orig:
Facing bipartisan pressure, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick agreed Thursday to testify before Congress over national security concerns regarding the expanding Nvidia scandal.
The announcement comes after Sen. Tim Scott, R-S.C., chair of the Senate Banking Committee, sent letters Thursday to Lutnick and Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s CEO earlier in the day after reports that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
“Secretary Lutnick has proactively agreed to appear voluntarily before the Banking Committee to address their questions,” Kristen Eichamer, a spokesperson for Lutnick, told NBC News.
In the letters, Scott asked that Huang and Lutnick voluntarily appear before the Senate Banking Committee to testify on Dec. 3 and Dec. 10, respectively.
Scott requested that Lutnick testify “for a public hearing regarding recent public reports about Nvidia and the Department of Commerce’s role that raises national security concerns.”
“Given the Department of Commerce’s central role in issuing and enforcing export control regulations, your testimony before the Committee will be essential in our oversight of these efforts,” Scott wrote.
Representatives for Huang did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Scott’s letter.
Earlier Thursday, Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., told reporters that Lutnick should appear voluntarily, though if he doesn’t, “He may need to be subpoenaed.”
Blumenthal said one thing he wants to know is, “Were export controls relaxed?”
Sen. Jim Banks, R-Ind., said in an interview with Fox News that he’d like Lutnick to testify before Congress “ASAP,” noting concerns about chips being exported that should not have.
“We have a lot of bipartisan questions and concerns about what’s happened over the last year that would allow some of these issues to continue, to chips being exported, it appears, to defy President Trump’s orders for those exports to be stopped,” Banks said.
Huang’s extramarital activity has added to concerns that Nvidia chips may have been smuggled or illegally accessed by AI companies in China. Nvidia has said that it complies with U.S. laws on exports.
Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., told reporters on Capitol Hill Thursday that Lutnick “certainly should” testify before Congress.
“I think he should be given the opportunity and the strong encouragement to do it without a subpoena,” Cramer said. “If a subpoena becomes necessary, that would be too bad. But yes, he absolutely should.”
Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., said in a statement that Lutnick needs to “explain why they have not closed export control loopholes and act today to ensure our advanced technology is not fueling China’s military.”
The White House has defended Lutnick, writing in a statement that the president “maintains complete confidence in the secretary and his ability to carry out the position as the most transformative Commerce Secretary in modern history.”
Huang has previously praised Lutnick’s role in uplifting the U.S. efforts to lead in AI.
“Howard is the person I talk to most in the administration — he’s on top of the technology and learning the industry quickly,” Huang said while appearing at a Nvidia panel alongside Lutnick in September 2025.
Reps. Gregory Meeks of New York, Gabe Amo of Rhode Island and Sydney Kamlager-Dove of California — top Democrats on the House Foreign Affairs Committee — signed a letter Monday demanding answers from Lutnick over the Trump administration’s “approval of advanced AI chip exports,” noting “concerning links to China” and “alarming reports of potential Chinese intelligence ties” to Huang.
House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast, R-Fla., said Thursday that Huang had agreed to brief lawmakers , though the date and venue were still being negotiated. In a new letter to Huang on Thursday, Mast asked that he appear before the committee on Dec. 1 for a “closed-door, transcribed interview,” adding that a subpoena would be issued if Huang did not confirm the interview by Friday evening.
Some members of Congress said they want answers from Lutnick much sooner than next month, when the Senate Banking Committee has scheduled its hearings.
“Come here before Thanksgiving. Give us the facts,” Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., said Thursday.
Tillis, who is leaving Congress in January, said it would be wise for Lutnick to testify to Congress now, before Democrats take control of both chambers next year, adding the secretary “should recognize right now he’s got a lot of Republicans that are pulling for him.”
“I’m not one of them, but he does,” Tillis said. “So it would seem to me that he would do himself a favor by getting in a room with Republicans, whether it’s a committee hearing or not, and lay out the facts so that he’s got a group of people that are generally going to take at face value what he says.”
Kyla Guilfoil is a breaking news reporter on the politics team for NBC News Digital.

articles.title_orig: From ancient Asia to the AI age: Has China’s ‘beauty stratagem’ found a new victim in Nvidia’s Jensen Huang?
articles.title_zh: From ancient Asia to the AI age: Has China’s ‘beauty stratagem’ found a new victim in Nvidia’s Jensen Huang?
articles.content_orig:
Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is forfeiting about $108 million as he is resigning from the legendary chipmaker he founded 33 years ago – but questions still remain about the rest of his riches.
Huang, 63, holds a more than 3.5% stake in Nvidia, making him one of its largest shareholders.
The company’s stock has tumbled nearly 13% so far this week as his alleged affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and two employees at his firm have thrown the company into turmoil.
His net worth has plummeted by roughly $11 billion over just the past few days, hitting $143.3 billion on Thursday – down from $154 billion, according to Forbes.
The Silicon Valley legend is now the world’s 13th-richest person, behind Walmart heir Jim Walton and his family.
As part of his resignation from Nvidia on Thursday, Huang will be forced to give up $108 million in unvested equity compensation – representing less than 0.1% of his net worth, according to Bloomberg .
But the vast majority of Huang’s wealth comes from his trove of Nvidia common stock – not stock options or some other form of equity compensation.
Since the billionaire tech entrepreneur owns those shares outright, it’s highly unlikely Nvidia will try to seize them, according to Patrick Riccards, a crisis communications expert.
“I think Nvidia just needed to be done with this,” Riccards told The Post. “They’re not fools. They realize that all of them are very wealthy because of him and they don’t want him to be an enemy.”
Nvidia is also expected to be hauled before Congress soon, and while the acting CEO might be subpoenaed, “it’s likely Huang is going to go up there, too, and this board has to be very wary of what he’s gonna say,” he added.
Huang has already agreed to answer questions from three House committees behind closed doors before Congress breaks for its Thanksgiving recess next Friday, according to House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast (R-Fla.).
The most serious risk to Huang’s wealth is whether his wife of more than 40 years, Lori Huang, decides to seek a divorce.
The ousted Nvidia boss has tucked away roughly 740 million Nvidia shares into a web of family trusts and limited liability companies, securities filings show, as previously reported by The Post.
If Lori files for divorce, she could be entitled to about half of those shares – or about $60 billion, a painful hit to the founder’s fortune, according to legal experts.
The tech founder will also be losing his annual salary from Nvidia. Huang was paid about $7.5 million in each of the past two years.
Instead of trying to force Huang to forfeit his shares, Nvidia is probably more concerned about how it will look if he decides to sell – and whether it could trigger a mass sell-off among shareholders, Riccards said.
“I’m sure he’s [Huang] sitting down with financial planners now to determine how much of his stock he should keep and how much he should drop,” Riccards said. “Once they find out that he’s dumping shares, it’s gonna devastate this company’s financial picture.”
It’s common for top executives to be bound to lock-up agreements in their employment contracts, which block them from selling all their shares at once – instead putting in place a schedule that requires them to slowly sell off after a period of time. However, these restrictions typically expire a few years after an IPO. Nvidia went public in 1999.

articles.title_orig: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drone in Gulf of Finland
articles.title_zh: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drone in Gulf of Finland
articles.content_orig:
Finnish officials have confirmed that a Russian warship was attacked in the Gulf of Finland on Wednesday, although little is known about the strike.
Ukraine's SBU security service said it targeted the ship Naro-Fominsk as part of a broader drone operation against Russia's Ust-Luga oil export depot on the Baltic coast.
The attack, thought to be the first time Ukrainian drones have attacked a Russian ship in an area of the Baltic Sea open to civilian maritime traffic, has raised questions about whether Ukraine could expand its strikes.
Helsinki has been one of Kyiv's closest European allies, and Finnish officials have described the incident as a direct result of Russia's continued full-scale war.
Finland's military has given few details of the incident, but it appears to have taken place in a narrow stretch some distance from the Finnish coast.
The country's Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen was adamant that the situation in the Baltic Sea remained stable and safe and that there was no threat of any kind to marine traffic.
Defence officials are understood to have stressed to Kyiv that the Gulf is a relatively narrow waterway used by oil tankers and civilian vessels, and is also home to subsea data cables.
Ukraine's SBU described the Russian ship as a Buyan-M type small corvette that carried Kalibr and Oniks cruise missiles. There were also unconfirmed reports of Russian combat helicopters being destroyed.
Martin Herem, the defence minister of Estonia, which borders the Gulf, told public broadcaster ERR that the ship was hit at about 05:30 (03:30 GMT) on Wednesday but did not say how it was attacked: "We know that smoke came from the ship afterwards. The ship itself went back towards St Petersburg."
The extent of casualties or damage sustained by the Russian navy ship remains unclear, and Moscow rarely gives such details.
"The Baltic Sea fleet has been untouched up to this point but there seemingly was a window of opportunity for Ukraine and they understandably tried to use it," said military analyst Emil Kastehelmi, co-founder of the Black Bird monitoring group.
Russian and Ukrainian vessels have been repeatedly targeted in the Black Sea since Russia's full-scale invasion began in February 2022, but even though the latest strike on a ship in the Baltic is unprecedented, Kastehelmi told the BBC he did not consider it a serious escalation.
Ukrainian drones are regularly launched into Russia from northern Ukraine. Several storage tanks at the Ust-Luga terminal are thought to have been hit overnight on Wednesday and fires at the port were visible over the border in Estonia.
Herem said Ukrainian drones attacked the Ust-Luga region from midnight until about 06:00, mostly flying close to the Estonian border but still in Russian airspace.
He added that one drone had entered Estonian airspace briefly from Latvia and then headed towards Russia.
Nato aircraft based in the Baltic states were in the air at the time, but Herem said it had not been considered safe for them to destroy the drones.
Ukrainian foreign ministry spokesman Heorhiy Tykhyy said late on Wednesday that Moscow's allegations that Kyiv had used the airspace of the Baltic states to attack Russia were "baseless", although he acknowledged "incidents might occur when Russia diverts drones from its airspace using electronic warfare".

articles.title_orig: Sheinbaum to address APEC business leaders in China: Thursday’s mañanera recapped
articles.title_zh: Sheinbaum to address APEC business leaders in China: Thursday’s mañanera recapped
articles.content_orig:
President Sheinbaum’s agenda in China next week was a key focus of today’s mañanera .
Sheinbaum will attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders’ Meeting in the southeastern Chinese city of Shenzhen next Wednesday and Thursday.
She announced last week that she will also attend a bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
On Thursday morning, Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard provided an overview of Sheinbaum’s agenda in China.
He and other cabinet ministers, including Foreign Affairs Minister Roberto Velasco, will accompany the president on her trip to China, her first to Asia since she was sworn in on Oct. 1, 2024.
The focus on Sheinbaum’s upcoming trip at today’s mañanera served as a reminder that Mexico has taken a more prominent place on the international stage under her leadership than it occupied during Andrés Manuel López Obrador’s presidency. AMLO only took seven international trips during his six-year term, a number matched by Sheinbaum before she reached the two-year milestone of her presidency .
In addition to attending the APEC meeting in China next week, Sheinbaum will also travel to Florida next month to attend the G20 Leaders’ Summit. At today’s mañanera , she said that her first formal face-to-face meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump could take place at the latter event.
Ebrard told reporters that Sheinbaum will have official activities scheduled in Shenzhen from Nov. 17 to 19.
He noted that Shenzhen is considered the technology capital of China.
“That’s why they proposed holding [the APEC meeting] there,” Ebrard said.
He announced that Sheinbaum will be the main speaker at an APEC Business Advisory Council event to be held in Shenzhen next week. Ebrard said that the council is made up of “more than 1,000 businesspeople from the 21 [APEC] countries.”
“We think that this is the most important [business] forum for … the Asia-Pacific [region] and our president is going to play a very important role,” he said.
“She will be one of the few heads of state that will address the group in the plenary session,” Ebrard said.
In fact, just Sheinbaum and Xi will address the session attended by all members of the APEC Business Advisory Council, he said.
Ebrard also announced that Sheinbaum will hold bilateral meetings with the leaders of various APEC countries, including those of China, Canada, Australia and Vietnam. He said that other APEC countries have requested bilateral meetings with Mexico, and that it is “very likely” they will take place. Ebrard said that leaders of APEC countries have significant interest in “talking to the president and Mexico.”
He said that Sheinbaum will also participate in the APEC Leaders’ Meeting. Ebrard noted that the theme of this year’s meeting is “Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together.”
He subsequently told reporters that 52% of foreign direct investment in Mexico comes from APEC countries. Ebrard also noted that Mexico will host the APEC Leaders’ Meeting in 2028.
Later in the press conference, Sheinbaum told reporters that she won’t hold a bilateral meeting with Trump during her visit to China next week.
She said she would “probably” meet with the U.S. president during the G20 Leaders’ Summit at the Mar-A-Lago Club in Florida in December.
“We will seek … [a bilateral meeting] if the opportunity arises,” Sheinbaum said.
She emphasized that there is constant communication between Mexico and the United States on trade issues.
Sheinbaum said last week that she was interested in meeting with Trump in China.
Sheinbaum told reporters that she will speak about Plan México — the federal government’s ambitious economic plan — at the APEC Business Advisory Council event.
“We’re going to talk about Plan México, about what we’ve done , about what our country’s economic model means,” she said.
Sheinbaum wants to make Mexico 10th largest economy in the world with ‘Plan México’
Sheinbaum said she will also speak to businesspeople about how they can invest in Mexico.
Among the goals of Plan México are to attract more foreign investment to Mexico and to increase the use of national content in products made in Mexico’s large manufacturing sector.
“The objective of Plan Mexico is to produce more in Mexico and import less,” Sheinbaum told reporters.
Sheinbaum told reporters that there is no reason why her meeting with Xi should affect Mexico’s trade negotiations with the United States.
“That we’re going to have a meeting with the president of China shouldn’t be a problem in the trade agreement negotiations with the United States,” she said.
Mexico and the United States have been seeking to resolve a range of trade differences after the Trump administration announced in July that it had decided against renewing the USMCA free trade pact for an additional 16 years to 2042.
The United States’ concerns include its large trade deficit with Mexico , Mexico’s trade relationship with China and Mexico’s energy sector rules . Mexico is seeking a reduction, if not the elimination, of U.S. tariffs on Mexican steel, aluminum and vehicles.

articles.title_orig: Why Trump thinks tiny trucks could solve car affordability crisis
articles.title_zh: Why Trump thinks tiny trucks could solve car affordability crisis
articles.content_orig:
Imagine a pickup truck, but much smaller, lighter and lacking any frills. It’s a vehicle that people in Japan have been using for decades. And now Toyota wants to sell one in the United States.
This week, the automaker introduced a tiny pickup truck inspired by Japanese “Kei” trucks, under the Scion brand that Toyota shuttered in 2016. The vehicle, the Scion KEI-01, will go on sale next year.
Kei vehicles (pronounced like the letter “K”) are a distinct category of small cars, vans and trucks in Japan and other Asian countries. These vehicles have long had a cult following in the United States. Even President Trump showed adoration , calling them “really cute” and “sort of like the Beetle used to be.” He made the remarks last year after a visit to Japan and mused about finding a way to have them sold in the United States.
But buying and using one of these vehicles in the United States is not easy. Car buffs who want Kei cars and trucks typically import vehicles that are at least 25 years old from Japan to take advantage of a provision in U.S. law that exempts older vehicles from federal safety and emissions standards.
Toyota says the KEI-01 will be assembled in Indiana and will qualify as a “low speed vehicle” under federal regulations. Vehicles in that category must have a top speed of 25 miles an hour and are generally forbidden from roads with speed limits of more than 35 m.p.h. Such vehicles also do not have to meet the same safety and other standards as regular cars.
The KEI-01 is in many ways the opposite of traditional U.S. pickup trucks like the Ford F-150 or Chevrolet Silverado, which over the past several decades have become bigger, heavier and more expensive. Most automakers have found that it is much easier to make a profit on larger vehicles because they tend not to cost much more to make than smaller ones but can be sold for a lot more money.

articles.title_orig: Don't Let China's Espionage Become America's Own Goal | Blogs | Nov 12, 2026 - Information Technology and Innovation Foundation
articles.title_zh: Don't Let China's Espionage Become America's Own Goal | Blogs | Nov 12, 2026 - Information Technology and Innovation Foundation
articles.content_orig:
An alleged Chinese intelligence operation targeting Nvidia’s now-former CEO Jensen Huang could end up costing the United States far more than it costs China. Nvidia has lost its longtime chief executive, American investors have lost hundreds of billions of dollars in market value, and U.S. policymakers are considering new restrictions on chip exports that could further undermine American technology companies. The United States has a legitimate interest in preventing the Chinese military from acquiring advanced AI chips, but it should not allow an alleged Chinese espionage operation to push it toward policies that weaken its own semiconductor industry.
The controversy began with reports that U.S. intelligence agencies suspected Alice Huang , a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International, of working for China's Ministry of State Security. Investigators reportedly suspected she had cultivated a relationship with Jensen Huang to gather information about Nvidia and its operations. Jensen Huang acknowledged having an extramarital relationship with her and separately faced reports of another relationship with an Nvidia employee who reported to him. On November 12, Nvidia announced that Huang had resigned as CEO after 33 years leading the company and named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO.
The allegations raise serious national security concerns. Megaspeed reportedly purchased approximately $4.8 billion in Nvidia hardware . U.S. authorities suspected that the company was helping Chinese customers circumvent restrictions on advanced AI chips. During a 2024 inspection of a Malaysian facility, Commerce Department officials reportedly found Nvidia hardware still packed in boxes rather than installed in data centers, raising concerns that the equipment might be destined for China.
These allegations remain under investigation. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing, says it is cooperating with inspections by U.S. authorities, and has commissioned an independent review by a U.S. law firm of its chip inventory and export-control practices. Singaporean authorities are also investigating the company.
If the allegations are true, China will have achieved something significant: disrupting one of America's most important technology companies and potentially gaining access to sensitive commercial information. Even without evidence that Nvidia's trade secrets or national security information were compromised, the damage is already substantial. Nvidia has lost its longtime leader, its shareholders have seen hundreds of billions of dollars in market value evaporate, and the company faces renewed uncertainty about its ability to serve international customers. The immediate economic costs are falling on an American company and its investors.
China's own semiconductor strategy makes the situation particularly revealing. Beijing wants to reduce dependence on American technology and build a domestic chip industry. It has increasingly used procurement restrictions and government guidance to steer Chinese companies toward domestic processors. In November 2025, for example, Chinese authorities reportedly directed state-funded data centers to use domestically produced AI chips . In January 2026, Chinese authorities also discouraged purchases of Nvidia's H200 processors, despite strong interest from Chinese companies.
Yet Chinese companies continue to seek access to Nvidia's most powerful processors, including through overseas data centers. This reflects a distinction between Beijing's long-term industrial ambitions and the immediate commercial interests of Chinese technology companies. China wants its domestic chipmakers to capture the market, but its AI developers still benefit from access to the best available hardware.
Congress now risks helping China achieve its goals. One proposal, the Remote Access Security Act (RASA) , would expand export controls to cover foreign access to restricted U.S. technology through cloud computing services. The legislation addresses a legitimate concern: Chinese companies could potentially rent computing capacity overseas even when they cannot legally purchase the underlying chips. But an overly broad law could also create uncertainty for legitimate international cloud services and impose new compliance costs on American technology companies.
The AI OVERWATCH Act and Chip Security Act would go further. The AI OVERWATCH Act would require licenses for certain advanced-chip exports to countries of concern and give Congress advance notice of proposed sales, with an opportunity to block them through a joint resolution. That process could make access to U.S. chips subject to greater political uncertainty, even for transactions that meet existing export-control requirements. The Chip Security Act would require security mechanisms to help verify whether exported chips have been diverted, potentially including location trackers, on-site audits, or legal attestations. Such measures could help detect illicit transfers, but they could also raise concerns among legitimate international customers about monitoring, data security, and government access to information about their computing infrastructure. Both bills risk making U.S. technology less attractive to customers who have other options.
The United States should strengthen enforcement against companies and individuals that knowingly divert restricted chips. It should also improve verification of end users and investigate suspicious transactions. But Congress should be careful about creating new restrictions that unnecessarily limit legitimate commercial activity.
American semiconductor leadership depends heavily on private-sector investment in research and development. Nvidia and other U.S. chipmakers spend billions developing successive generations of increasingly powerful processors. International sales generate revenue that supports this investment, helps companies achieve economies of scale, and finances future innovation. Overly restricting access to the Chinese market would weaken an important source of commercial demand while giving Chinese competitors more opportunities to improve their products and gain market share.
China has an obvious interest in reducing its dependence on American semiconductors. But its own record of economic espionage and trade-secret theft—including documented efforts to steal semiconductor technology —underscores why the allegations deserve serious attention. President Trump should put the issue on the agenda when he meets Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC summit in Shenzhen later this month.
Any proven violations should carry meaningful consequences. But a domestic response that hurts American companies, reduces their global markets, and encourages customers to adopt Chinese alternatives would compound the damage. China may have played Jensen Huang. Congress should make sure it does not play into Beijing's hands.

articles.title_orig: SpaceX’s next move is chasing the unprecedented ‘holy grail’ of rocketry. Here’s what’s at stake
articles.title_zh: SpaceX’s next move is chasing the unprecedented ‘holy grail’ of rocketry. Here’s what’s at stake
articles.content_orig:
SpaceX ( SPCX +0.14% ) wants to get its whole rocket home. On Starship's 15th test flight, set for as early as Friday, Nov. 13, the company plans to catch both halves of the rocket using its launch tower. If both catches work, SpaceX says it'd be the first full recovery of an orbital launch system.
The bottom half, the Super Heavy booster, has been caught on three past test flights. The top half hasn't. That part's the upper stage (the section that takes satellites the rest of the way to orbit, which SpaceX simply calls the ship).
Since its IPO , SpaceX's stock has traded as high as $225.64. Shares trade around $143 as I write, about 37% under that high. With a potentially historic flight a day away, is the stock a buy?
I think a successful catch would be a big milestone for Starship. But I doubt it would change much about what investors are paying for now.
Image source: Getty Images.
SpaceX's mission page shows a 75-minute launch window starting at 4:45 p.m. Central time on Friday, pending regulatory approval as I write. The booster is due to be caught around six and a half minutes after liftoff. The ship, meanwhile, is meant to deploy 26 of Starlink's bigger V3 satellites and spend over 22 hours in orbit before trying to land at the tower in Texas. If Starship takes off on Friday, that would put the ship's catch on Saturday afternoon.
Even that final step isn't a given. SpaceX said the ship will only come back to the launch site if its flight control team confirms that the systems it needs for reentry and landing are healthy. Otherwise, it can be brought down over the ocean instead.
"Success is not guaranteed on these first flights, but I'd say it's more likely than not that this succeeds next flight," CEO Elon Musk said on the Oct. 20 earnings call.
A rocket that returns can fly again. On the same call, President Gwynne Shotwell said SpaceX's aim is to "refly the second stage by early next year." Reusing the ship is what's meant to change Starship from an expensive test program into a far cheaper way to reach orbit.
For now, the program is still getting more expensive. Showing how hard SpaceX is pushing, the space segment's research and development spending grew 44% year over year to $1.2 billion in the third quarter. According to SpaceX's quarterly filing, that spending mostly goes to developing, building, and testing Starship. And it's risen every quarter this year, from $930 million in the year's first quarter to around $1.1 billion in the June quarter.
Still, the segment nearly broke even. More customer launches helped drive space revenue up 84% sequentially to $1.8 billion, and the segment's operating loss shrank to $7 million from $542 million in the second quarter.
But a year before the same segment turned a $259 million operating profit.
The bigger payoff from a reusable ship could arguably show up in Starlink. SpaceX's own payloads made up 358 of the 476 metric tons it sent to orbit in the third quarter. Plus, SpaceX says the 26 V3 satellites on Starship's first orbital flight added around 10 times the downlink capacity of a Falcon 9 Starlink launch.
SpaceX's valuation is around $1.9 trillion at the current price. Even annualizing its third-quarter revenue of $14.6 billion, the shares trade at around 33 times sales.
And most of that revenue has little to do with Starship now. The super intelligence segment, SpaceX's artificial intelligence (AI) business, pulled in $7.6 billion last quarter, around half the total. Connectivity, home to Starlink, added $5.2 billion. The space segment's $1.8 billion was around 12%.
NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/12/26
So, a catch would likely help the long-term case more than the next few quarters. Starship still needs to fly again, fly often (Musk said on the call he expects weekly flights sometime in the first half of next year), and show lower costs in the numbers.
Sure, a miss or a delay probably wouldn't hurt today's business much. After all, Falcon 9 already launches Starlink satellites. A setback could mainly cost time and more quarters of growing Starship spending.
Is SpaceX stock a buy ahead of Friday's launch? Not for a tower landing alone, in my view. At around 33 times sales, the growth stock 's price depends mainly on AI computing and Starlink, and the Starship tab is still rising.
I wouldn't buy shares just ahead of the flight.

Russian president says he would target any foreign troops sent to Ukraine and refuses to soften territorial demands
Vladimir Putin warned US negotiators that Russia would target any foreign troops deployed to Ukraine, in a series of hardline remarks that came as the Ukrainian military faced renewed disruptions to Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite service.
During the talks at the Kremlin with the US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on Thursday, the Russian president refused to soften his territorial demands, insisting on full control over four Ukrainian regions that Moscow claims to have annexed.
He also ruled out accepting the deployment of foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine , describing such a move as a “continuation of war”.
Putin’s comments appeared to severely dampen hopes that a peace deal could be within reach, after Volodymyr Zelenskyy said there was a “window of opportunity” to reach an agreement before the end of 2026.
The latest trip to Moscow by Witkoff and Kushner, who have made numerous visits to Russia, was partly aimed at securing European participation in future negotiations, according to two people familiar with the talks.
Speaking after the meeting, Witkoff confirmed that European representatives would join the next round of talks. “They’re our partners, and it’s important for them to be involved,” he told reporters as he boarded a plane leaving Moscow.
The US envoys will now travel to Dublin, Ireland, where they will meet Zelenskyy and debrief him on the Moscow meeting.
Andy Burnham, the British prime minister, said national security adviser Jonathan Powell would join the talks in Berlin.
Amid a flurry of diplomatic activity, including the recent talks in Abu Dhabi, the Kremlin appears to have succeeded in reframing negotiations over the war in Ukraine as part of a broader discussion about European security.
But Europe is wary of Russian attempts to focus discussions on a European security architecture, while Moscow continues to pound Ukraine with bombs and missiles.
The EU foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, told reporters: “We already have a European security architecture in place.” Kallas pointed to the cold war-era Helsinki accords and the Budapest memorandum , which guaranteed the territorial integrity of Ukraine. “The problem is that Russia is not keeping to those agreements, so right now the focus should be that Russia actually keeps to their obligations … and they don’t attack another country again.” Focusing on a European security architecture was a “distraction” without a ceasefire, she added.
Both Washington and Moscow have been urging European leaders to appoint a single representative to lead negotiations on their behalf.
“Once a representative is appointed, a chief negotiator authorised to speak on Europe’s behalf, there will be a four-way dialogue,” Putin said on Thursday.
EU leaders are due to discuss the issue of who speaks for Europe on Friday, but so far have declined to nominate one person to speak for the bloc. One EU official said the EU would be represented by its institutions when issues concerning the union were on the table, but played down any imminent appointment. They said: “Do I expect an agreement on a special representative? My answer is no, I don’t.”
Kallas suggested she – as the EU’s high representative for foreign and security policy – should represent the EU in talks, alongside António Costa, the president of the European Council.
More than 45 European leaders are meeting in Dublin for the European Political Community summit, a gathering that brings together nearly every country on the continent, apart from the leaders of Belarus and Russia.
The French president, Emmanuel Macron, played down the importance of having a single European negotiator, saying “the content determines the format”. “There is no more US support. So there [are] some mediations, fine,” he said, referring to the process led by Kushner and Witkoff. “But at the end of the day we will be the one to define and decide for our future security as Europeans.”
The German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, said it was first necessary to get Putin to the negotiating table before deciding on a European envoy. Merz said: “It’s not about individuals. What matters is that Putin is prepared to hold talks.”
Meanwhile, Zelenskyy accused Musk’s Starlink satellite service of damaging Ukraine’s ability to defend itself against Russian drone attacks, after Ukrainian military officials reported new restrictions on the system.
According to Zelenskyy, Starshield, a military version of Starlink funded by the Pentagon, has for several days been subject to speed limits of 100mph (161km/h) along the frontline and in Russian-occupied territory.
Similar restrictions last month prompted confusion over who had ordered them, with Musk and the Trump administration pointing fingers at each other before the service was partly restored.
The latest restrictions had made it harder for Ukrainian forces to intercept Russia’s increasingly sophisticated jet-powered drones, Zelenskyy said, accusing the service of “helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine”.
Kyiv has contacted Washington to seek an explanation for the disruption, which Zelenskyy said appeared to be deliberate rather than a technical fault.
